sentences.zh: 高祖始受命，鉏類夷荒，天下略定，即詔有司立周公、孔子廟於國學，四時祠。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu first received the Mandate, he uprooted disorder and pacified the wilderness; once the realm was largely settled, he immediately ordered the relevant offices to establish temples to the Duke of Zhou and Confucius at the Directorate of Education, with sacrifices in all four seasons.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu first took the throne, he cleared away chaos and pacified the frontier lands. Once the empire was largely at peace, he ordered officials to establish temples to the Duke of Zhou and Confucius at the Imperial Academy, with sacrifices in all four seasons.

sentences.zh: 求其後，議加爵土。

translations.literal: He sought their descendants and deliberated on granting them titles and fiefs.
translations.idiomatic: He sought out their descendants and debated granting them titles and fiefs.

sentences.zh: 國學始置生七十二員，取三品以上子、弟若孫為之；

translations.literal: The Directorate of Education first established seventy-two student places, drawn from sons, younger brothers, or grandsons of officials of the third rank and above;
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Academy initially enrolled seventy-two students, selected from sons, younger brothers, or grandsons of officials of the third rank and above;

sentences.zh: 太學百四十員，取五品以上；

translations.literal: the Imperial University one hundred forty places, drawn from the fifth rank and above;
translations.idiomatic: the Imperial University one hundred forty, drawn from the fifth rank and above;

sentences.zh: 四門學百三十員，取七品以上。

translations.literal: the Four Gates Academy one hundred thirty places, drawn from the seventh rank and above.
translations.idiomatic: and the Four Gates Academy one hundred thirty, drawn from the seventh rank and above.

sentences.zh: 郡縣三等，上郡學置生六十員，中、下以十為差；

translations.literal: Prefectures and counties were divided into three grades: upper prefectures established sixty student places, middle and lower ones differing by ten;
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures and counties were ranked in three grades: upper prefectures set aside sixty student places, with middle and lower grades differing by ten;

sentences.zh: 上縣學置生四十員，中、下亦以十為差。

translations.literal: upper counties established forty student places, middle and lower ones also differing by ten.
translations.idiomatic: upper counties set aside forty student places, with middle and lower grades again differing by ten.

sentences.zh: 又詔宗室、功臣子孫就秘書外省，別為小學。

translations.literal: He also ordered imperial clansmen and descendants of meritorious ministers to attend a separate primary school at the outer Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered members of the imperial clan and descendants of meritorious ministers to attend a separate primary school at the outer Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 太宗身櫜，風纚露沐，然銳情經術，即王府開文學館，召名儒十八人為學士，與議天下事。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong bore arms on his person, braved wind and dew, yet keenly devoted himself to the classics; at his princely residence he opened a Literary Academy, summoned eighteen renowned Confucians as academicians, and deliberated on affairs of the realm with them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong went to war with bow at his side and braved wind and rain, yet he was passionately devoted to the classics. At his princely residence he opened a Literary Academy, summoned eighteen renowned Confucians as academicians, and discussed affairs of state with them.

sentences.zh: 既即位，殿左置弘文館，悉引內學士番宿更休；

translations.literal: After he took the throne, he placed the Hongwen Hall to the left of the palace hall and brought in all the inner academicians to rotate night duty;
translations.idiomatic: After his accession, he established the Hongwen Hall to the left of the throne hall and brought in all the inner academicians to rotate night duty;

sentences.zh: 聽朝之間，則與討古今，道前王所以成敗，或日昃夜艾，未嘗少怠。

translations.literal: between audiences he would discuss past and present with them, expounding how former kings succeeded or failed, sometimes until the sun slanted and night deepened, never slackening even slightly.
translations.idiomatic: between audiences he would discuss past and present with them, explaining how earlier rulers had succeeded or failed—sometimes until sunset and deep into the night, never slackening.

sentences.zh: 貞觀六年，詔罷周公祠，更以孔子為先聖，顏氏為先師，盡召天下惇師老德以為學官。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhenguan, an edict abolished sacrifices to the Duke of Zhou and instead made Confucius the Sage and the Yan clan the Exemplary Teacher; all the most reverent and venerable teachers under Heaven were summoned to serve as school officials.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the Zhenguan era, an edict abolished sacrifices to the Duke of Zhou and instead made Confucius the Sage and the Yan clan the Exemplary Teacher. All the most respected teachers in the realm were summoned to serve as school officials.

sentences.zh: 數臨幸觀釋菜，命祭酒博士講論經義，賜以束帛。

translations.literal: He repeatedly visited in person to observe the ceremonial offering of vegetables, ordered the libationer and erudites to expound the classics, and bestowed bundles of silk.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly visited in person to observe the ceremonial offering of vegetables, ordered the libationer and erudites to expound the classics, and bestowed bundles of silk.

sentences.zh: 生能通一經者，得署吏。

translations.literal: Students who could master one classic were permitted to be appointed as clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Students who could master one classic were permitted to be appointed as clerks.

sentences.zh: 廣學舍千二百區，三學益生員，並置書、算二學，皆有博士。

translations.literal: School quarters were expanded to twelve hundred units; the three academies increased their student quotas, and Schools of Writing and Calculation were also established, each with erudites.
translations.idiomatic: School quarters were expanded to twelve hundred units; the three academies increased their enrollments, and Schools of Writing and Calculation were also established, each with erudites.

sentences.zh: 大抵諸生員至三千二百。

translations.literal: In general the student quota reached three thousand two hundred.
translations.idiomatic: In all, student enrollment reached three thousand two hundred.

sentences.zh: 自玄武屯營飛騎，皆給博士受經，能通一經者，聽入貢限。

translations.literal: From the Xuanwu garrison and the Flying Cavalry, all were assigned erudites to receive instruction in the classics; those who could master one classic were allowed to enter the tribute quota.
translations.idiomatic: Even the Xuanwu garrison and the Flying Cavalry were assigned erudites to teach them the classics; those who mastered one classic were allowed to enter the tribute quota.

sentences.zh: 四方秀艾，挾策負素，坌集京師，文治煟然勃興。

translations.literal: Outstanding talents from the four quarters, bearing writing tablets and carrying scrolls, thronged the capital; literary governance flourished and rose vigorously.
translations.idiomatic: Outstanding talents from every quarter, bearing writing tablets and carrying scrolls, thronged the capital, and literary governance flourished with new vigor.

sentences.zh: 於是新羅、高昌、百濟、吐蕃、高麗等群酋長並遣子弟入學，鼓笥踵堂者，凡八千餘人。

translations.literal: Thereupon chieftains of Silla, Gaochang, Baekje, Tibet, Goguryeo, and others all sent their sons and younger brothers to study; those who beat their book-cases and followed one another into the hall numbered more than eight thousand in all.
translations.idiomatic: Chieftains of Silla, Gaochang, Baekje, Tibet, Goguryeo, and other states all sent their sons and younger brothers to study. Those who beat their book-cases and followed one another into the hall numbered more than eight thousand in all.

sentences.zh: 紆侈袂，曳方履，訚訚秩秩，雖三代之盛，所未聞也。

translations.literal: With flowing sleeves and square-toed shoes, orderly and dignified in manner—such splendor, even in the flourishing age of the Three Dynasties, had never been heard of.
translations.idiomatic: With flowing sleeves and square-toed shoes, orderly and dignified in manner—such splendor had never been heard of, even in the flourishing age of the Three Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 帝又讎正《五經》繆闕，頒天下示學者，與諸儒稡章句為義疏，俾久其傳。

translations.literal: The emperor also collated errors and omissions in the Five Classics and distributed them throughout the realm to show scholars; together with the Confucians he compiled commentaries and explications, so that the tradition might long endure.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also collated errors and omissions in the Five Classics and distributed them throughout the realm for scholars. Together with the Confucians he compiled commentaries and explications so that the tradition might long endure.

sentences.zh: 因詔前代通儒梁皇偘、褚仲都、周熊安生、沈重、陳沈文阿、周弘正、張譏、隋何妥、劉炫等子孫，並加引擢。

translations.literal: Accordingly he ordered the descendants of former generations' master Confucians—Liang Huang Kan, Chu Zhongdu, Zhou Xiong Ansheng, Shen Chong, Chen Shen Wen'a, Zhou Hongzheng, Zhang Ji, Sui He Tuo, Liu Xuan, and others—to be promoted and elevated.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered the descendants of master Confucians of earlier generations—Liang Huang Kan, Chu Zhongdu, Zhou Xiong Ansheng, Shen Chong, Chen Shen Wen'a, Zhou Hongzheng, Zhang Ji, Sui He Tuo, Liu Xuan, and others—to be promoted and elevated.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，詔「左丘明、卜子夏、公羊高、穀梁赤、伏勝、高堂生、戴聖、毛萇、孔安國、劉向、鄭眾、杜子春、馬融、盧植、鄭玄、服虔、何休、王肅、王弼、杜預、範寧二十一人，用其書，行其道，宜有以褒大之，自今並配享孔子廟廷」。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, an edict stated: "Zuo Qiuming, Bu Zixia, Gongsun Gao, Guliang Chi, Fu Sheng, Gaotang Sheng, Dai Sheng, Mao Chang, Kong Anguo, Liu Xiang, Zheng Zhong, Du Zichun, Ma Rong, Lu Zhi, Zheng Xuan, Fu Qian, He Xiu, Wang Su, Wang Bi, Du Yu, and Fan Ning—twenty-one men who used their books and practiced their ways—should be honored and magnified; from now on they shall all share sacrifice in the court of Confucius's temple."
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year, an edict declared: "Zuo Qiuming, Bu Zixia, Gongsun Gao, Guliang Chi, Fu Sheng, Gaotang Sheng, Dai Sheng, Mao Chang, Kong Anguo, Liu Xiang, Zheng Zhong, Du Zichun, Ma Rong, Lu Zhi, Zheng Xuan, Fu Qian, He Xiu, Wang Su, Wang Bi, Du Yu, and Fan Ning—twenty-one men whose books were used and whose ways were followed—deserve to be honored and magnified. From now on they shall all share sacrifice in the court of Confucius's temple."

sentences.zh: 於是唐三百年之盛，稱貞觀，寧不其然。

translations.literal: Thus the splendor of Tang's three hundred years was called Zhenguan—is this not so?
translations.idiomatic: Thus the splendor of Tang's three hundred years was called the Zhenguan era—is this not so?

sentences.zh: 高宗尚吏事，武後矜權變，至諸王駙馬，皆得領祭酒。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong valued administrative affairs; Empress Wu prided herself on expedient adaptation; even imperial princes and imperial sons-in-law were permitted to serve as libationers.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong valued administrative affairs; Empress Wu prided herself on expedient adaptation; even imperial princes and imperial sons-in-law were permitted to serve as libationers.

sentences.zh: 初，孔穎達等始署官，發《五經》題與諸生酬問；

translations.literal: At first, when Kong Yingda and others were first appointed to office, they issued Five Classics questions and exchanged answers with the students;
translations.idiomatic: At first, when Kong Yingda and others were first appointed to office, they issued Five Classics questions and exchanged answers with the students;

sentences.zh: 及是，惟判祥瑞案三牒即罷。

translations.literal: by this time they merely adjudicated three dossiers of auspicious omens and then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: by this time they merely adjudicated three dossiers of auspicious omens and then ceased.

sentences.zh: 玄宗詔群臣及府郡舉通經士，而褚無量、馬懷素等勸講禁中，天子尊禮，不敢盡臣之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong ordered ministers and prefectures to recommend men versed in the classics, while Chu Wuliang, Ma Huaisu, and others lectured within the palace; the Son of Heaven honored them with ceremony and did not dare treat them wholly as subjects.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong ordered ministers and prefectures to recommend men versed in the classics, while Chu Wuliang, Ma Huaisu, and others lectured within the palace. The Son of Heaven honored them with ceremony and did not dare treat them wholly as subjects.

sentences.zh: 置集賢院部分典籍、乾元殿博匯群書至六萬卷，經籍大備，又稱開元焉。

translations.literal: The Jixian Academy was established to organize the classics; the Qianyuan Hall broadly gathered books until they reached sixty thousand scrolls—the classics were fully stocked, and this too was called the Kaiyuan era.
translations.idiomatic: The Jixian Academy was established to organize the classics; the Qianyuan Hall broadly gathered books until they reached sixty thousand scrolls. The classics were fully stocked, and this too was called the Kaiyuan era.

sentences.zh: 祿山之禍，兩京所藏，一為炎埃，官私楮，喪脫幾盡，章甫之徒，劫為縵胡。

translations.literal: In the disaster of Lushan, what the two capitals had stored was turned to ash and dust; official and private paper was lost almost entirely; those who wore the scholar's cap were plundered like barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: In the disaster of Lushan, what the two capitals had stored was turned to ash and dust; official and private paper was lost almost entirely; scholars were plundered like barbarians.

sentences.zh: 於是嗣帝區區救亂未之得，安暇語貞觀、開元事哉？

translations.literal: Thereupon the succeeding emperor, struggling merely to quell disorder, had not yet succeeded—how could he spare time to speak of Zhenguan and Kaiyuan affairs?
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the succeeding emperor, struggling merely to quell disorder, had not yet succeeded—how could he spare time to speak of Zhenguan and Kaiyuan affairs?

sentences.zh: 自楊綰、鄭餘慶、鄭覃等以大儒輔政，議優學科，先經誼，黜進士，後文辭，亦弗能克也。

translations.literal: From Yang Wan, Zheng Yuqing, Zheng Tan, and others, who as great Confucians assisted in government and debated favoring the classical examination, putting classical meaning first, demoting the jinshi degree, and subordinating literary composition—they too could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Even when Yang Wan, Zheng Yuqing, Zheng Tan, and other great Confucians assisted in government and debated favoring the classical examination—putting classical meaning first, demoting the jinshi degree, and subordinating literary composition—they too could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 文宗定《五經》，镵之石，張參等是正訛文，寥寥一二可紀。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong fixed the Five Classics, carved them in stone; Zhang Can and others corrected erroneous texts—only one or two things worth recording remain.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong fixed the Five Classics and carved them in stone; Zhang Can and others corrected erroneous texts—only one or two things worth recording remain.

sentences.zh: 由是觀之，始未嘗不成於艱難，而後敗於易也。

translations.literal: Viewed thus, beginnings were never achieved except through hardship, while later ruin came through ease.
translations.idiomatic: Viewed thus, beginnings were never achieved except through hardship, while later ruin came through ease.

sentences.zh: 嘗論之，武為救世砭劑，文其膏粱歟！

translations.literal: It has been argued: military affairs are the needle that saves the age; are literary affairs its rich fare?
translations.idiomatic: It has been argued: military affairs are the needle that saves the age; are literary affairs its rich fare?

sentences.zh: 亂已定，必以文治之。

translations.literal: Once disorder is settled, governance by culture is indispensable.
translations.idiomatic: Once disorder is settled, governance by culture is indispensable.

sentences.zh: 否者，是病損而進砭劑，其傷多矣！

translations.literal: Otherwise, it is like advancing the needle when the illness has already damaged the body—the harm will be great!
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, it is like advancing the needle when the illness has already damaged the body—the harm will be great!

sentences.zh: 然則武得之，武治之，不免霸且盜，聖人反是而王。

translations.literal: Thus if military power obtains and military power governs, one cannot escape being merely hegemonic and predatory; the sage reverses this and becomes king.
translations.idiomatic: Thus if military power obtains and military power governs, one cannot escape being merely hegemonic and predatory; the sage reverses this and becomes king.

sentences.zh: 故曰武創業，文守成，百世不易之道也。

translations.literal: Therefore it is said: military affairs found the enterprise, cultural affairs preserve it—an unchanging way for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore it is said: military affairs found the enterprise, cultural affairs preserve it—an unchanging way for a hundred generations.

sentences.zh: 若乃舉天下一之於仁義，莫若儒。

translations.literal: If one is to unite all under Heaven in benevolence and righteousness, nothing surpasses Confucianism.
translations.idiomatic: If one is to unite all under Heaven in benevolence and righteousness, nothing surpasses Confucianism.

sentences.zh: 儒待其人，乃能光明厥功，宰相大臣是已。

translations.literal: Confucianism awaits the right person before its achievements can shine forth—prime ministers and great officials are such.
translations.idiomatic: Confucianism awaits the right person before its achievements can shine forth—prime ministers and great officials are such.

sentences.zh: 至專誦習傳授、無它大事業者，則次為《儒學篇》。

translations.literal: As for those who specialize in recitation, transmission, and instruction without other great achievements, they are recorded next in the "Confucian Scholars" chapters.
translations.idiomatic: As for those who specialize in recitation, transmission, and instruction without other great achievements, they are recorded next in the "Confucian Scholars" chapters.

sentences.zh: 徐曠，字文遠，以字行。

translations.literal: Xu Kuang, styled Wenyuan, was known by his style name.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Kuang, styled Wenyuan, was known by his style name.

sentences.zh: 南齊司空孝嗣五世孫。

translations.literal: He was a fifth-generation descendant of Xiao Qi's Minister of Works Xiaosi of Southern Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He was a fifth-generation descendant of Minister of Works Xiaosi of Southern Qi.

sentences.zh: 父徹，梁秘書郎，尚元帝女安昌公主。

translations.literal: His father Che served as Secretary Gentleman of Liang and married Princess Anchang, daughter of Emperor Yuan of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Che served as Secretary Gentleman of Liang and married Princess Anchang, daughter of Emperor Yuan of Liang.

sentences.zh: 江陵陷，俘以西，客偃師，貧不能自給。

translations.literal: When Jiangling fell, he was taken captive westward, lodged in Yanshi, and was too poor to support himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangling fell, he was taken captive westward, lodged in Yanshi, and was too poor to support himself.

sentences.zh: 兄文林鬻書於肆，文遠日閱之，因博通《五經》，明《左氏春秋》。

translations.literal: His elder brother Wenlin sold books in a shop; Wenyuan daily perused them and thereby mastered the Five Classics and was accomplished in the Zuo clan's Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Wenlin sold books in a shop; Wenyuan daily perused them and thereby mastered the Five Classics and became accomplished in the Zuo clan's Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 時耆儒沈重講太學，授業常千人，文遠從之質問，不數日辭去。

translations.literal: At the time the venerable Confucian Shen Chong lectured at the Imperial University, his disciples often numbering a thousand; Wenyuan went to question him but departed within a few days.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the venerable Confucian Shen Chong lectured at the Imperial University, his disciples often numbering a thousand; Wenyuan went to question him but departed within a few days.

sentences.zh: 或問其故，答曰：「先生所說，紙上語耳。

translations.literal: When someone asked the reason, he replied: "What the master speaks is merely words on paper.
translations.idiomatic: When someone asked the reason, he replied: "What the master speaks is merely words on paper.

sentences.zh: 若奧境，彼有所未見者，尚何觀？」

translations.literal: If there are hidden depths, and he has not yet seen them, what is there to observe?"
translations.idiomatic: If there are hidden depths he has not yet seen, what is there to observe?"

sentences.zh: 重知其語，召與反復研辯，嗟嘆其能。

translations.literal: Shen Chong understood his meaning, summoned him for repeated study and debate, and sighed in admiration of his ability.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Chong understood his meaning, summoned him for repeated study and debate, and sighed in admiration of his ability.

sentences.zh: 性方正，舉動純重，竇威、楊玄感、李密、王世充皆從受學。

translations.literal: By nature upright and square, his conduct pure and weighty, Dou Wei, Yang Xuangan, Li Mi, and Wang Shichong all studied under him.
translations.idiomatic: By nature upright and square, his conduct pure and weighty, Dou Wei, Yang Xuangan, Li Mi, and Wang Shichong all studied under him.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇中，累遷太學博士，詔與漢王諒授經。

translations.literal: In the Kaihuang era of Sui, he was repeatedly promoted to Erudite of the Imperial University and ordered to instruct the Prince of Han, Liang, in the classics.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaihuang era of Sui, he was repeatedly promoted to Erudite of the Imperial University and ordered to instruct Prince Liang of Han in the classics.

sentences.zh: 會諒反，除名為民。

translations.literal: When Liang rebelled, he was stripped of office and made a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang rebelled, he was stripped of office and made a commoner.

sentences.zh: 大業初，禮部侍郎許善心薦文遠及包愷、褚徽、陸德明、魯達為學官，擢國子博士，愷等為太學博士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Daye era, Vice Minister of Rites Xu Shanshan recommended Wenyuan together with Bao Kai, Chu Hui, Lu Deming, and Lu Da as school officials; Wenyuan was promoted to Erudite of the Directorate of Education, and Kai and the others to erudites of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Daye era, Vice Minister of Rites Xu Shanshan recommended Wenyuan together with Bao Kai, Chu Hui, Lu Deming, and Lu Da as school officials. Wenyuan was promoted to Erudite of the Directorate of Education, and Kai and the others to erudites of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 世稱《左氏》有文遠，《禮》有褚徽，《詩》有魯達，《易》有陸德明，皆一時冠雲。

translations.literal: The age said: for the Zuo tradition there was Wenyuan; for the Rites there was Chu Hui; for the Odes there was Lu Da; for the Changes there was Lu Deming—all at the time topped the clouds.
translations.idiomatic: The age said: for the Zuo tradition there was Wenyuan; for the Rites there was Chu Hui; for the Odes there was Lu Da; for the Changes there was Lu Deming—all at the time stood above their peers.

sentences.zh: 文遠說經，遍舉先儒異論，分明是非，乃出新意以折衷，聽者忘勞。

translations.literal: When Wenyuan expounded the classics, he comprehensively cited earlier Confucians' differing views, clearly distinguished right from wrong, and then brought forth new ideas to reconcile them; listeners forgot fatigue.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenyuan expounded the classics, he comprehensively cited earlier Confucians' differing views, clearly distinguished right from wrong, and then brought forth new ideas to reconcile them; listeners forgot their fatigue.

sentences.zh: 越王侗署國子祭酒。

translations.literal: Prince Tong of Yue appointed him Libationer of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Tong of Yue appointed him Libationer of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 時洛陽饑，文遠自出城樵拾，為李密所得。

translations.literal: At the time Luoyang suffered famine; Wenyuan went out of the city himself to gather firewood and was captured by Li Mi.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Luoyang suffered famine; Wenyuan went out of the city himself to gather firewood and was captured by Li Mi.

sentences.zh: 密使文遠南向坐，備弟子禮拜之，文遠謝曰：「前日以先王之道授將軍，今將軍擁兵百萬，威振四海，猶能屈體老夫，此盛德也，安敢不盡？

translations.literal: Mi had Wenyuan sit facing south and performed the rites of a disciple in bowing to him; Wenyuan declined, saying: "Formerly I taught the General the way of the former kings; now the General commands a million troops and his authority shakes the four seas, yet still can humble himself before this old man—this is great virtue. How dare I not do my utmost?
translations.idiomatic: Mi had Wenyuan sit facing south and performed the rites of a disciple in bowing to him. Wenyuan declined, saying: "Formerly I taught the General the way of the former kings; now the General commands a million troops and his authority shakes the four seas, yet still can humble himself before this old man—this is great virtue. How dare I not do my utmost?

sentences.zh: 將軍若欲為伊、霍，繼絕扶傾，吾雖老，猶願盡力；

translations.literal: If the General wishes to be like Yi Yin and Huo Guang, continuing the extinguished and supporting the tottering, though I am old I am still willing to exert myself to the full;
translations.idiomatic: If the General wishes to be like Yi Yin and Huo Guang, continuing the extinguished and supporting the tottering, though I am old I am still willing to exert myself to the full;

sentences.zh: 如為莽、卓，乘危迫險，則仆耄矣，無能為也！」

translations.literal: but if you act like Wang Mang or Dong Zhuo, seizing crisis to force peril, then I am aged and can do nothing!"
translations.idiomatic: but if you act like Wang Mang or Dong Zhuo, seizing crisis to force peril, then I am aged and can do nothing!"

sentences.zh: 密頓首曰：「幸得位上公，思所以竭力，先征化及刷國恥，然後入見天子，請罪於有司，惟先生教之。」

translations.literal: Mi bowed his head to the ground and said: "Fortunately I have attained the rank of Grand Duke; I think how to exert myself to the full—first to campaign against Huaji and wash away the national shame, then to enter and see the Son of Heaven and request punishment from the relevant offices. I rely on the Master's instruction."
translations.idiomatic: Mi bowed his head to the ground and said: "Fortunately I have attained the rank of Grand Duke; I think how to exert myself to the full—first to campaign against Huaji and wash away the national shame, then to enter and see the Son of Heaven and request punishment from the relevant offices. I rely on the Master's instruction."

sentences.zh: 答曰：「將軍，名臣子，累世盡節，前陷玄感黨，迷未遠而復，今若終之以忠，天下之人所望於將軍者。」

translations.literal: He replied: "The General is the son of a renowned minister; for generations your house has exhausted its loyalty. Formerly you fell into Xuangan's faction, strayed but not far and returned; if now you end in loyalty, this is what all under Heaven expect of the General."
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "The General is the son of a renowned minister; for generations your house has exhausted its loyalty. Formerly you fell into Xuangan's faction, strayed but not far and returned; if now you end in loyalty, this is what all under Heaven expects of the General."

sentences.zh: 密頓首曰：「恭聞命。」

translations.literal: Mi bowed his head to the ground and said: "I respectfully receive the command."
translations.idiomatic: Mi bowed his head to the ground and said: "I respectfully receive the command."

sentences.zh: 俄而世充專制，密又問焉，對曰：「彼殘忍而意褊促，必速於亂，將軍非破之不可以朝。」

translations.literal: Before long Shichong seized sole power; Mi questioned him again, and he replied: "That man is cruel and his intent narrow and urgent; disorder will come quickly. The General cannot attend court unless you defeat him."
translations.idiomatic: Before long Shichong seized sole power; Mi questioned him again, and he replied: "That man is cruel and his intent narrow and urgent; disorder will come quickly. The General cannot attend court unless you defeat him."

sentences.zh: 密曰：「常謂先生儒者，不學軍旅，至籌大計，乃明略過人。」

translations.literal: Mi said: "I always considered the Master a Confucian who did not study military affairs; yet in planning great strategy his clear design surpasses others."
translations.idiomatic: Mi said: "I always considered the Master a Confucian who did not study military affairs; yet in planning great strategy his clear design surpasses others."

sentences.zh: 密敗，復入東都。

translations.literal: When Mi was defeated, he again entered the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Mi was defeated, he again entered the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 世充給稍異等，而文遠見輒先拜。

translations.literal: Shichong supplied him with slightly inferior provisions, yet whenever Wenyuan saw him he would bow first.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong supplied him with slightly inferior provisions, yet whenever Wenyuan saw him he would bow first.

sentences.zh: 或問：「君踞見李密而下王公，何邪？」

translations.literal: Someone asked: "You sat erect when you saw Li Mi yet bow to princes and dukes—why?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked: "You sat erect when you saw Li Mi yet bow to princes and dukes—why?"

sentences.zh: 答曰：「密，君子，能受酈生之揖；

translations.literal: He replied: "Mi is a gentleman and can accept Li Yiji's bow;
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "Mi is a gentleman and can accept Li Yiji's bow;

sentences.zh: 世充，小人，無容故人義。

translations.literal: Shichong is a petty man and has no room for the righteousness owed an old acquaintance.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong is a petty man and has no room for the righteousness owed an old acquaintance.

sentences.zh: 相時而動可也。」

translations.literal: One acts according to the times."
translations.idiomatic: One acts according to the times."

sentences.zh: 世充僭號，以為國子博士。

translations.literal: When Shichong usurped the title, he was made Erudite of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: When Shichong usurped the title, he was made Erudite of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 子士會奔長安，世充怒，絕其稟，文遠餓幾死，數矣。

translations.literal: His son Shihui fled to Chang'an; Shichong in anger cut off his stipend; Wenyuan nearly starved to death several times.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shihui fled to Chang'an; Shichong in anger cut off his stipend; Wenyuan nearly starved to death several times.

sentences.zh: 身出樵，為羅士信所獲，送京師，仍為國子博士。

translations.literal: Going out himself to gather firewood, he was captured by Luo Shixin, sent to the capital, and again made Erudite of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Going out himself to gather firewood, he was captured by Luo Shixin, sent to the capital, and again made Erudite of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 高祖幸國學觀釋奠，文遠發《春秋》題，論難鋒生，隨方占對，莫能屈。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu visited the Directorate of Education to observe the ceremonial offering, Wenyuan issued a Spring and Autumn question; the keen students debated, and he responded according to each point—none could overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu visited the Imperial Academy to observe the ceremonial offering, Wenyuan issued a Spring and Autumn question; the keen students debated, and he responded according to each point—none could overcome him.

sentences.zh: 帝異之，封東莞縣男。

translations.literal: The emperor marveled at this and enfeoffed him as Baron of Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor marveled at this and enfeoffed him as Baron of Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十四。

translations.literal: He died at the age of seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 孫有功，自有傳。

translations.literal: His grandson Yougong has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Yougong has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 陸元朗，字德明，以字行，蘇州吳人。

translations.literal: Lu Yuanlang, styled Deming, was known by his style name; he was a native of Wu in Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yuanlang, styled Deming, was known by his style name; he was a native of Wu in Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 善名理言，受學於周弘正。

translations.literal: He was skilled in Neo-Daoist discourse and studied under Zhou Hongzheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled in Neo-Daoist discourse and studied under Zhou Hongzheng.

sentences.zh: 陳太建中，後主為太子，集名儒入講承光殿，德明始冠，與下坐。

translations.literal: In the Taojian era of Chen, when the Later Lord was crown prince, he gathered renowned Confucians to lecture in Chengguang Hall; Deming had just reached adulthood and sat among the lower seats.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taojian era of Chen, when the Later Lord was crown prince, he gathered renowned Confucians to lecture in Chengguang Hall; Deming had just reached adulthood and sat among the lower seats.

sentences.zh: 國子祭酒徐孝克敷經，倚貴縱辯，眾多下之，獨德明申答，屢奪其說，舉坐咨賞。

translations.literal: The libationer Xu Xiaoke expounded the classics, relying on his rank to debate freely; the multitude mostly yielded, but Deming alone answered and repeatedly seized his arguments; the whole assembly sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: The libationer Xu Xiaoke expounded the classics, relying on his rank to debate freely; the multitude mostly yielded, but Deming alone answered and repeatedly seized his arguments; the whole assembly sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 解褐始興國左常侍。

translations.literal: Upon leaving office he was appointed Left Regular Attendant of the Principality of Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: Upon leaving office he was appointed Left Regular Attendant of the Principality of Shixing.

sentences.zh: 陳亡，歸鄉闬。

translations.literal: When Chen fell, he returned to his native district.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen fell, he returned to his native district.

sentences.zh: 隋煬帝擢秘書學士。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang of Sui promoted him to Secretariat Academician.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang of Sui promoted him to Secretariat Academician.

sentences.zh: 大業間，廣召經明士，四方踵至。

translations.literal: During the Daye era, men versed in the classics were broadly summoned, and they came from the four quarters in succession.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye era, men versed in the classics were broadly summoned, and they came from the four quarters in succession.

sentences.zh: 於是德明與魯達、孔褒共會門下省相酬難，莫能詘。

translations.literal: Thereupon Deming together with Lu Da and Kong Bao met at the Secretariat to exchange challenges, and none could defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Deming together with Lu Da and Kong Bao met at the Secretariat to exchange challenges, and none could defeat them.

sentences.zh: 遷國子助教。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Assistant Instructor of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Assistant Instructor of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 越王侗署為司業，入殿中授經。

translations.literal: Prince Tong of Yue appointed him as Vice Director and had him enter the hall to instruct in the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Tong of Yue appointed him as Vice Director and had him enter the hall to instruct in the classics.

sentences.zh: 王世充僭號，封子玄恕為漢王，以德明為師，即其廬行束脩禮。

translations.literal: When Wang Shichong usurped the title, he enfeoffed his son Xuanshu as Prince of Han and made Deming his teacher; at his dwelling he performed the ceremony of presenting dried meat.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shichong usurped the title, he enfeoffed his son Xuanshu as Prince of Han and made Deming his teacher; at his dwelling he performed the ceremony of presenting dried meat.

sentences.zh: 德明恥之，服巴豆劑，僵偃東壁下。

translations.literal: Deming was shamed by this; he took a croton purgative and lay stiff on the east wall.
translations.idiomatic: Deming was shamed by this; he took a croton purgative and lay stiff on the east wall.

sentences.zh: 玄恕入拜床垂，德明對之遺利，不復開口，遂移病成臯。

translations.literal: Xuanshu entered to bow at the bedside; Deming faced him and soiled himself, no longer opening his mouth, and then feigned illness at Chenggao.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanshu entered to bow at the bedside; Deming faced him and soiled himself, no longer opening his mouth, and then feigned illness at Chenggao.

sentences.zh: 世充平，秦王辟為文學館學士，以經授中山王承乾，補太學博士。

translations.literal: When Shichong was pacified, the Prince of Qin recruited him as an academician of the Literary Academy, had him instruct Prince Chengqian of Zhongshan in the classics, and appointed him Erudite of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: When Shichong was pacified, the Prince of Qin recruited him as an academician of the Literary Academy, had him instruct Prince Chengqian of Zhongshan in the classics, and appointed him Erudite of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 高祖已釋奠，召博士徐文遠、浮屠慧乘、道士劉進喜各講經，德明隨方立義，遍析其要。

translations.literal: After Emperor Gaozu had performed the ceremonial offering, he summoned the erudites Xu Wenyuan, the Buddhist Huicheng, and the Daoist Liu Jinxi each to expound a classic; Deming established meaning according to each school and comprehensively analyzed their essentials.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Gaozu had performed the ceremonial offering, he summoned the erudites Xu Wenyuan, the Buddhist Huicheng, and the Daoist Liu Jinxi each to expound a classic; Deming established meaning according to each school and comprehensively analyzed their essentials.

sentences.zh: 帝大喜曰：「三人者誠辯，然德明一舉輒蔽，可謂賢矣！」

translations.literal: The emperor greatly rejoiced and said: "These three men are indeed eloquent, yet Deming with one stroke covers them all—he may be called worthy!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor greatly rejoiced and said: "These three men are indeed eloquent, yet Deming with one stroke covers them all—he may be called worthy!"

sentences.zh: 賜帛五十匹，遷國子博士，封吳縣男。

translations.literal: He bestowed fifty bolts of silk, promoted him to Erudite of the Directorate of Education, and enfeoffed him as Baron of Wu County.
translations.idiomatic: He bestowed fifty bolts of silk, promoted him to Erudite of the Directorate of Education, and enfeoffed him as Baron of Wu County.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 論撰甚多，傳於世。

translations.literal: His treatises and compositions were many and passed down in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His treatises and compositions were many and passed down in the world.

sentences.zh: 後太宗閱其書，嘉德明博辯，以布帛二百段賜其家。

translations.literal: Later Emperor Taizong read his books, praised Deming's broad learning and eloquence, and bestowed two hundred bolts of silk on his family.
translations.idiomatic: Later Emperor Taizong read his books, praised Deming's broad learning and eloquence, and bestowed two hundred bolts of silk on his family.

sentences.zh: 子敦信，麟德中，繇左侍極檢校右相，累封嘉興縣子，以老疾致仕，終大司成。

translations.literal: His son Dunxin, in the Linde era, rose from Left Attendant-in-Ordinary inspecting the Right Chancellor to be repeatedly enfeoffed as Viscount of Jiaxing; he retired for old age and illness and ended as Grand Master of the Grand Academy.
translations.idiomatic: His son Dunxin, in the Linde era, rose from Left Attendant-in-Ordinary inspecting the Right Chancellor to be repeatedly enfeoffed as Viscount of Jiaxing; he retired for old age and illness and ended as Grand Master of the Grand Academy.

sentences.zh: 曹憲，揚州江都人。

translations.literal: Cao Xian was a native of Jiangdu in Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Xian was a native of Jiangdu in Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 仕隋為秘書學士，聚徒教授凡數百人，公卿多從之遊。

translations.literal: Serving Sui as Secretariat Academician, he gathered disciples to teach—several hundred in all—and many ministers and officials studied with him.
translations.idiomatic: Serving Sui as Secretariat Academician, he gathered disciples to teach—several hundred in all—and many ministers and officials studied with him.

sentences.zh: 於小學家尤邃，自漢杜林、衛宏以後，古文亡絕，至憲復興。

translations.literal: He was especially accomplished among scholars of small learning; since Du Lin and Wei Hong of Han, ancient script had been lost, and it was revived through Xian.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially accomplished among scholars of small learning; since Du Lin and Wei Hong of Han, ancient script had been lost, and it was revived through Xian.

sentences.zh: 煬帝令與諸儒撰《桂苑珠叢》，規正文字。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang ordered him together with the Confucians to compile the Guiyuan Zhucong and to standardize written characters.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang ordered him together with the Confucians to compile the Guiyuan Zhucong and to standardize written characters.

sentences.zh: 又註《廣雅》，學者推其該，藏於秘書。

translations.literal: He also annotated the Guangya; scholars praised its comprehensiveness, and it was stored in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He also annotated the Guangya; scholars praised its comprehensiveness, and it was stored in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，揚州長史李襲譽薦之，以弘文館學士召，不至，即家拜朝散大夫，當世榮之。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan era, Prefect Li Xiyu of Yangzhou recommended him; he was summoned as academician of the Hongwen Hall but did not come; he was appointed at home as Grand Master of the Palace and the age honored him.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenguan era, Prefect Li Xiyu of Yangzhou recommended him; he was summoned as academician of the Hongwen Hall but did not come; he was appointed at home as Grand Master of the Palace and the age honored him.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘗讀書，有奇難字，輒遣使者問憲，憲具為音註，援驗詳復，帝咨尚之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong was reading and encountered strange and difficult characters, he would send an envoy to ask Xian; Xian fully provided phonetic annotations and verified them in detail, and the emperor admired him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong was reading and encountered strange and difficult characters, he would send an envoy to ask Xian; Xian fully provided phonetic annotations and verified them in detail, and the emperor admired him.

sentences.zh: 卒，年百餘歲。

translations.literal: He died at the age of more than one hundred.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of more than one hundred.

sentences.zh: 憲始以梁昭明太子《文選》授諸生，而同郡魏模、公孫羅、江夏李善相繼傳授，於是其學大興。

translations.literal: Xian first taught Crown Prince Zhaoming of Liang's Wenxuan to his students; Wei Mo, Gongsun Luo, and Li Shan of the same commandery transmitted it in succession, and thereby the study greatly flourished.
translations.idiomatic: Xian first taught Crown Prince Zhaoming of Liang's Wenxuan to his students; Wei Mo, Gongsun Luo, and Li Shan of the same commandery transmitted it in succession, and thereby the study greatly flourished.

sentences.zh: 句容許淹者，自浮屠還為儒，多識廣聞，精故訓，與羅等並名家。

translations.literal: Xu Yan of Jurong, having returned from Buddhism to Confucianism, was widely learned, skilled in ancient glosses, and together with Luo and others was renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yan of Jurong, having returned from Buddhism to Confucianism, was widely learned, skilled in ancient glosses, and together with Luo and others was renowned.

sentences.zh: 羅官沛王府參軍事、無錫丞。

translations.literal: Luo served as Administrative Assistant in the Princely Household of Pei and as Assistant Magistrate of Wuxi.
translations.idiomatic: Luo served as Administrative Assistant in the Princely Household of Pei and as Assistant Magistrate of Wuxi.

sentences.zh: 模，武後時為左拾遺，子景倩亦世其學，以拾遺召，後歷度支員外郎。

translations.literal: Mo, in Empress Wu's time, was Left Remonstrator; his son Jingqian also inherited the learning and was summoned as Remonstrator, later serving as Outer Office Member of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Mo, in Empress Wu's time, was Left Remonstrator; his son Jingqian also inherited the learning and was summoned as Remonstrator, later serving as Outer Office Member of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 善，見子邕傳。

translations.literal: Shan is treated in the biography of his son Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Shan is treated in the biography of his son Yong.

sentences.zh: 顏師古，字籀，其先瑯邪臨沂人。

translations.literal: Yan Shigu, styled Zhou, was originally from Linyi in Langye.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shigu, styled Zhou, was originally from Linyi in Langye.

sentences.zh: 祖之推，自高齊入周，終隋黃門郎，遂居關中，為京兆萬年人。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhitui entered Zhou from Northern Qi and ended as Yellow Gate Gentleman of Sui; he then settled in Guanzhong and became a native of Wannian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhitui entered Zhou from Northern Qi and ended as Yellow Gate Gentleman of Sui; he then settled in Guanzhong and became a native of Wannian in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 父思魯，以儒學顯。

translations.literal: His father Silu was prominent for Confucian learning.
translations.idiomatic: His father Silu was prominent for Confucian learning.

sentences.zh: 武德初，為秦王府記室參軍事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wude he served as Administrative Assistant in the Princely Household of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Wude he served as Administrative Assistant in the Princely Household of Qin.

sentences.zh: 師古少博覽，精故訓學，善屬文。

translations.literal: Shigu from youth was broadly read, accomplished in ancient glosses, and skilled in literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Shigu from youth was broadly read, accomplished in ancient glosses, and skilled in literary composition.

sentences.zh: 仁壽中，李綱薦之，授安養尉。

translations.literal: In the Renshou era, Li Gang recommended him and he was appointed Magistrate of Anyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the Renshou era, Li Gang recommended him and he was appointed Magistrate of Anyang.

sentences.zh: 尚書左僕射楊素見其年弱，謂曰：「安養，劇縣。

translations.literal: Left Vice Minister of Works Yang Su saw how young he was and said: "Anyang is a difficult county.
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Minister of Works Yang Su saw how young he was and said: "Anyang is a difficult county.

sentences.zh: 子何以治之？」

translations.literal: With what will you govern it?"
translations.idiomatic: With what will you govern it?"

sentences.zh: 師古曰：「割雞未用牛刀。」

translations.literal: Shigu said: "To slaughter a chicken one need not use an ox-knife."
translations.idiomatic: Shigu said: "To slaughter a chicken one need not use an ox-knife."

sentences.zh: 素驚其言大，後果以幹治聞。

translations.literal: Su was startled by his bold words; later he indeed became known for capable administration.
translations.idiomatic: Su was startled by his bold words; later he indeed became known for capable administration.

sentences.zh: 時薛道衡為襄州總管，與之推舊，佳其才，每作文章，令指摘疵短。

translations.literal: At the time Xue Daoheng was Grand Prefect of Xiangzhou and, being old acquaintances, admired his talent; whenever he composed an essay he had Shigu point out its flaws.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Xue Daoheng was Grand Prefect of Xiangzhou and, being old acquaintances, admired his talent; whenever he composed an essay he had Shigu point out its flaws.

sentences.zh: 俄失職，歸長安，不得調，窶甚，資教授為生。

translations.literal: Before long he lost his post, returned to Chang'an, could not obtain reassignment, was extremely impoverished, and supported himself by teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he lost his post, returned to Chang'an, could not obtain reassignment, was extremely impoverished, and supported himself by teaching.

sentences.zh: 高祖入關，謁見長春宮，授朝散大夫，拜敦煌公府文學，累遷中書舍人，專典機密。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu entered the Pass, he had an audience at Changchun Palace, was appointed Grand Master of the Palace, became Literary Officer of the Princely Household of Dunhuang, and was repeatedly promoted to Secretariat Draftsman, exclusively managing confidential matters.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu entered the Pass, he had an audience at Changchun Palace, was appointed Grand Master of the Palace, became Literary Officer of the Princely Household of Dunhuang, and was repeatedly promoted to Secretariat Draftsman, exclusively managing confidential matters.

sentences.zh: 師古性敏給，明練治體。

translations.literal: Shigu was by nature quick and clever, clearly versed in the principles of governance.
translations.idiomatic: Shigu was by nature quick and clever, clearly versed in the principles of governance.

sentences.zh: 方軍國務多，詔令一出其手，冊奏之工，當時未有及者。

translations.literal: When military and state affairs were many, edicts and orders came from his hand; the craftsmanship of memorials and documents—at the time none could match him.
translations.idiomatic: When military and state affairs were many, edicts and orders came from his hand; the craftsmanship of memorials and documents—at the time none could match him.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，拜中書侍郎，封瑯邪縣男，以母喪解。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong took the throne, he was appointed Vice Minister of the Secretariat and enfeoffed as Baron of Langye; he resigned on account of his mother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong took the throne, he was appointed Vice Minister of the Secretariat and enfeoffed as Baron of Langye; he resigned on account of his mother's mourning.

sentences.zh: 服除，還官。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he returned to office.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended, he returned to office.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，坐公事免。

translations.literal: After more than a year, he was dismissed for a public matter.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year, he was dismissed for a public matter.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗嘆《五經》去聖遠，傳習浸訛，詔師古於秘書省考定，多所厘正。

translations.literal: The emperor once sighed that the Five Classics were far from the sages and that transmission and study had gradually erred; he ordered Shigu to examine and fix them at the Secretariat, correcting many points.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once sighed that the Five Classics were far from the sages and that transmission and study had gradually erred; he ordered Shigu to examine and fix them at the Secretariat, correcting many points.

sentences.zh: 既成，悉詔諸儒議，於是各執所習，共非詰師古。

translations.literal: When completed, all the Confucians were summoned to debate; each clung to what he had learned and together criticized Shigu.
translations.idiomatic: When completed, all the Confucians were summoned to debate; each clung to what he had learned and together criticized Shigu.

sentences.zh: 師古輒引晉、宋舊文，隨方曉答，誼據該明，出其悟表，人人嘆服。

translations.literal: Shigu then cited Jin and Song old texts, answering according to each point; his meaning and evidence were comprehensive and clear, exceeding their understanding; everyone sighed in submission.
translations.idiomatic: Shigu then cited Jin and Song old texts, answering according to each point; his meaning and evidence were comprehensive and clear, exceeding their understanding; everyone sighed in submission.

sentences.zh: 尋加通直郎、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally appointed General of Unimpeded Access and Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was additionally appointed General of Unimpeded Access and Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 帝因頒所定書於天下，學者賴之。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon distributed the fixed books throughout the realm, and scholars relied on them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereupon distributed the fixed books throughout the realm, and scholars relied on them.

sentences.zh: 俄拜秘書少監，專刊正事，古篇奇字世所惑者，討析申孰，必暢本源。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat, exclusively engaged in collation; for ancient texts and strange characters that perplexed the world, he analyzed and clarified them and always expounded the original source.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat, exclusively engaged in collation; for ancient texts and strange characters that perplexed the world, he analyzed and clarified them and always expounded the original source.

sentences.zh: 然多引後生與讎校，抑素流，先貴勢，雖商賈富室子，亦竄選中，由是素議薄之，斥為郴州刺史。

translations.literal: Yet he often brought in young men for collation, suppressed common scholars, and favored the noble and powerful first; even sons of merchant families were smuggled into selection, and thereby common opinion slighted him; he was demoted to Prefect of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he often brought in young men for collation, suppressed common scholars, and favored the noble and powerful first; even sons of merchant families were smuggled into selection, and thereby common opinion slighted him; he was demoted to Prefect of Chen.

sentences.zh: 未行，帝惜其才，讓曰：「卿之學，信可稱者，而事親居官，朕無聞焉。

translations.literal: Before he departed, the emperor, cherishing his talent, reproached him: "Your learning can indeed be praised, yet in serving parents and holding office I have heard nothing of you.
translations.idiomatic: Before he departed, the emperor, cherishing his talent, reproached him: "Your learning can indeed be praised, yet in serving parents and holding office I have heard nothing of you.

sentences.zh: 今日之行，自誰取之？

translations.literal: Today's departure—who chose it?
translations.idiomatic: Today's departure—who chose it?

sentences.zh: 念卿曩經任使，朕不忍棄，後宜自戒。」

translations.literal: Considering your past appointments and service, I cannot bear to abandon you; hereafter you should warn yourself."
translations.idiomatic: Considering your past appointments and service, I cannot bear to abandon you; hereafter you should warn yourself."

sentences.zh: 師古謝罪，復留為故官。

translations.literal: Shigu apologized for his fault and was again retained in his former office.
translations.idiomatic: Shigu apologized for his fault and was again retained in his former office.

sentences.zh: 師古性簡峭，視輩行傲然，罕所推接。

translations.literal: Shigu was by nature terse and sharp, looked on his peers with arrogance, and rarely promoted or received others.
translations.idiomatic: Shigu was by nature terse and sharp, looked on his peers with arrogance, and rarely promoted or received others.

sentences.zh: 既負其才，早見驅策，意望甚高。

translations.literal: Having relied on his talent and early been driven forward, his expectations were very high.
translations.idiomatic: Having relied on his talent and early been driven forward, his expectations were very high.

sentences.zh: 及是頻被譴，仕益不進，罔然喪沮，乃闔門謝賓客，巾褐裙帔，放情蕭散，為林墟之適。

translations.literal: When he was repeatedly reprimanded, his advancement in office grew no further; despondent and discouraged, he closed his gates to guests, wore cloth cap and skirt, let himself go in carefree ease, and found pleasure in woodland and wilderness.
translations.idiomatic: When he was repeatedly reprimanded, his advancement in office grew no further; despondent and discouraged, he closed his gates to guests, wore cloth cap and skirt, let himself go in carefree ease, and found pleasure in woodland and wilderness.

sentences.zh: 多藏古圖畫、器物、書帖，亦性所篤愛。

translations.literal: He collected many ancient paintings, artifacts, and calligraphic scrolls—this too was what his nature deeply loved.
translations.idiomatic: He collected many ancient paintings, artifacts, and calligraphic scrolls—this too was what his nature deeply loved.

sentences.zh: 與撰《五禮》成，進爵為子。

translations.literal: Participating in the compilation of the Five Rites, he was advanced in rank to Viscount.
translations.idiomatic: Participating in the compilation of the Five Rites, he was advanced in rank to Viscount.

sentences.zh: 又為太子承乾註班固《漢書》上之，賜物二百段、良馬一，時人謂杜征南、顏秘書為左丘明、班孟堅忠臣。

translations.literal: He also annotated Ban Gu's Book of Han for Crown Prince Chengqian and presented it; he was bestowed two hundred bolts of goods and one fine horse. Men of the time called Du Zhennan and Secretary Yan the loyal ministers of Zuo Qiuming and Ban Mengjian.
translations.idiomatic: He also annotated Ban Gu's Book of Han for Crown Prince Chengqian and presented it; he was bestowed two hundred bolts of goods and one fine horse. Men of the time called Du Zhennan and Secretary Yan the loyal ministers of Zuo Qiuming and Ban Mengjian.

sentences.zh: 帝將有事泰山，詔公卿博士雜定其儀，而論者爭為異端。

translations.literal: When the emperor was about to perform the feng and shan rites on Mount Tai, he ordered ministers, erudites, and others jointly to fix the ritual; debaters contended and made divergent ends.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was about to perform the feng and shan rites on Mount Tai, he ordered ministers, erudites, and others jointly to fix the ritual; debaters contended and made divergent ends.

sentences.zh: 師古奏：「臣撰定《封禪儀註書》在十一年，於時諸儒謂為適中。」

translations.literal: Shigu memorialized: "Your subject compiled the Fengshan Yizhu Book in the eleventh year; at the time the Confucians said it was moderate."
translations.idiomatic: Shigu memorialized: "Your subject compiled the Fengshan Yizhu Book in the eleventh year; at the time the Confucians said it was moderate."

sentences.zh: 於是以付有司，多從其說。

translations.literal: Thereupon it was handed to the relevant offices, and they mostly followed his sayings.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon it was handed to the relevant offices, and they mostly followed his sayings.

sentences.zh: 遷秘書監、弘文館學士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Secretariat and academician of the Hongwen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Director of the Secretariat and academician of the Hongwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 十九年，從征遼，道病卒，年六十五，謚曰戴。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he followed the campaign against Liaodong, fell ill on the road, and died at the age of sixty-five; his posthumous title was Dai.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he followed the campaign against Liaodong, fell ill on the road, and died at the age of sixty-five; his posthumous title was Dai.

sentences.zh: 其所註《漢書》、《急就章》大顯於時。

translations.literal: His annotations on the Book of Han and the Jijiuzhang greatly shone in the age.
translations.idiomatic: His annotations on the Book of Han and the Jijiuzhang greatly shone in the age.

sentences.zh: 永徽三年，子揚廷為符璽郎，表上師古所撰《匡謬正俗》八篇。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yonghui, his son Yangting, as Gentleman of the Talisman Office, submitted the eight chapters of Kuangmiu Zhengsu that Shigu had compiled.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yonghui, his son Yangting, as Gentleman of the Talisman Office, submitted the eight chapters of Kuangmiu Zhengsu that Shigu had compiled.

sentences.zh: 初，思魯與妻不相宜，師古苦諫，父不聽，情有所隔，故帝及之。

translations.literal: At first Silu and his wife were not compatible; Shigu bitterly remonstrated but his father would not listen, and affection was divided—therefore the emperor mentioned this.
translations.idiomatic: At first Silu and his wife were not compatible; Shigu bitterly remonstrated but his father would not listen, and affection was divided—therefore the emperor mentioned this.

sentences.zh: 師古弟相時，字睿，亦以學聞。

translations.literal: Shigu's younger brother Xiangshi, styled Rui, was also renowned for learning.
translations.idiomatic: Shigu's younger brother Xiangshi, styled Rui, was also renowned for learning.

sentences.zh: 為天策府參軍事。

translations.literal: He served as Administrative Assistant in the Heavenly Strategy Princely Household.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Administrative Assistant in the Heavenly Strategy Princely Household.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，累遷諫議大夫，有爭臣風。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan era he was repeatedly promoted to Remonstrator of the Left and had the manner of a disputing minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenguan era he was repeatedly promoted to Remonstrator of the Left and had the manner of a disputing minister.

sentences.zh: 轉禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 羸瘠多病。」

translations.literal: Emaciated and often ill."
translations.idiomatic: Emaciated and often ill."

sentences.zh: 師古死，不勝哀而卒。

translations.literal: When Shigu died, he could not bear the grief and also died.
translations.idiomatic: When Shigu died, he could not bear the grief and also died.

sentences.zh: 師古叔遊秦，武德初，累遷廉州刺史，封臨沂縣男。

translations.literal: Shigu's uncle Youqin, at the beginning of Wude, was repeatedly promoted to Prefect of Lianzhou and enfeoffed as Baron of Linyi.
translations.idiomatic: Shigu's uncle Youqin, at the beginning of Wude, was repeatedly promoted to Prefect of Lianzhou and enfeoffed as Baron of Linyi.

sentences.zh: 時劉黑闥初平，人多強暴，比遊秦至，禮讓大行，邑裏歌之，高祖下璽書獎勞。

translations.literal: When Liu Heita had just been pacified, many people were violent; when Youqin arrived, courtesy and yielding greatly prevailed, and the district sang of him; Emperor Gaozu issued an imperial letter of reward and encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Heita had just been pacified, many people were violent; when Youqin arrived, courtesy and yielding greatly prevailed, and the district sang of him; Emperor Gaozu issued an imperial letter of reward and encouragement.

sentences.zh: 終鄆州刺史。

translations.literal: He ended as Prefect of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He ended as Prefect of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 撰《漢書決疑》，師古多資取其義。

translations.literal: He compiled Jueyi on the Book of Han; Shigu largely drew on its meaning.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled Jueyi on the Book of Han; Shigu largely drew on its meaning.

sentences.zh: 孔穎達，字仲達，冀州衡水人。

translations.literal: Kong Yingda, styled Zhongda, was a native of Hengshui in Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Yingda, styled Zhongda, was a native of Hengshui in Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 八歲就學，誦記日千餘言，暗記《三禮義宗》。

translations.literal: At eight he began study; he could recite more than a thousand words daily and memorized in secret the Three Rites Yizong.
translations.idiomatic: At eight he began study; he could recite more than a thousand words daily and memorized in secret the Three Rites Yizong.

sentences.zh: 及長，明服氏《春秋傳》、鄭氏《尚書》、《詩》、《禮記》、王氏《易》，善屬文，通步歷。

translations.literal: When grown, he was accomplished in Fu clan's Spring and Autumn Commentary, Zheng clan's Documents, Odes, and Record of Rites, and Wang clan's Changes; he was skilled in literary composition and versed in step-calendars.
translations.idiomatic: When grown, he was accomplished in the Fu clan's Spring and Autumn Commentary, Zheng clan's Documents, Odes, and Record of Rites, and Wang clan's Changes; he was skilled in literary composition and versed in step-calendars.

sentences.zh: 嘗造同郡劉焯，焯名重海內，初不之禮，及請質所疑，遂大畏服。

translations.literal: He once visited Liu Zhuo of the same commandery; Zhuo was renowned throughout the realm and at first did not treat him with ceremony; when Yingda requested to question what he doubted, Zhuo then greatly feared and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He once visited Liu Zhuo of the same commandery; Zhuo was renowned throughout the realm and at first did not treat him with ceremony; when Yingda requested to question what he doubted, Zhuo then greatly feared and submitted.

sentences.zh: 隋大業初，舉明經高第，授河內郡博士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daye in Sui, he passed the mingjing examination with high rank and was appointed Erudite of Henei Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Daye in Sui, he passed the mingjing examination with high rank and was appointed Erudite of Henei Commandery.

sentences.zh: 煬帝召天下儒官集東都，詔國子秘書學士與論議，穎達為冠，又年最少，老師宿儒恥出其下，陰遣客刺之，匿楊玄感家得免。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang summoned Confucians from all under Heaven to gather at the Eastern Capital and ordered Secretariat academicians of the Directorate of Education to debate with them; Yingda took first place and was also the youngest; old teachers and established Confucians were shamed to rank below him and secretly sent assassins; he hid in Yang Xuangan's house and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang summoned Confucians from all under Heaven to gather at the Eastern Capital and ordered Secretariat academicians of the Directorate of Education to debate with them. Yingda took first place and was also the youngest; old teachers and established Confucians were shamed to rank below him and secretly sent assassins; he hid in Yang Xuangan's house and escaped.

sentences.zh: 補太學助教。

translations.literal: He was appointed Assistant Instructor of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Assistant Instructor of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 隋亂，避地虎牢。

translations.literal: When Sui fell into disorder, he took refuge at Hulao.
translations.idiomatic: When Sui fell into disorder, he took refuge at Hulao.

sentences.zh: 太宗平洛，授文學館學士，遷國子博士。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong pacified Luoyang, he was appointed academician of the Literary Academy and transferred to Erudite of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong pacified Luoyang, he was appointed academician of the Literary Academy and transferred to Erudite of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，封曲阜縣男，轉給事中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan he was enfeoffed as Baron of Qufu and transferred to Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhenguan he was enfeoffed as Baron of Qufu and transferred to Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 時帝新即位，穎達數以忠言進。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor had newly taken the throne; Yingda repeatedly offered loyal words.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the emperor had newly taken the throne; Yingda repeatedly offered loyal words.

sentences.zh: 帝問：「孔子稱『以能問於不能，以多問於寡，有若無，實若虛』，何謂也？」

translations.literal: The emperor asked: "Confucius said 'though able, ask those who cannot; though having much, ask those who have little; having as if not having, full as if empty'—what does this mean?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked: "Confucius said 'though able, ask those who cannot; though having much, ask those who have little; having as if not having, full as if empty'—what does this mean?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「此聖人教人謙耳。

translations.literal: He replied: "This is the sage teaching people humility.
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "This is the sage teaching people humility.

sentences.zh: 己雖能，仍就不能之人以咨所未能；

translations.literal: Though oneself able, still consult those who cannot about what one has not yet mastered;
translations.idiomatic: Though oneself able, still consult those who cannot about what one has not yet mastered;

sentences.zh: 己雖多，仍就寡少之人更資其多。

translations.literal: though oneself having much, still go to those with little and further seek their abundance.
translations.idiomatic: though oneself having much, still go to those with little and further seek their abundance.

sentences.zh: 內有道，外若無；

translations.literal: Within there is the Way, outwardly as if none;
translations.idiomatic: Inwardly one holds the Way, yet outwardly one appears to have nothing;

sentences.zh: 中雖實，容若虛。

translations.literal: inwardly though full, outwardly as if empty.
translations.idiomatic: though inwardly full, one presents oneself as if empty.

sentences.zh: 非特匹夫，君德亦然。

translations.literal: This applies not only to common men—the virtue of a ruler is likewise.
translations.idiomatic: This is true not only of ordinary men—the virtue of a ruler follows the same rule.

sentences.zh: 故《易》稱『蒙以養正』，『明夷以蒞眾』。

translations.literal: Therefore the Changes says 'Meng uses correctness to nurture' and 'Mingyi uses obscurity to govern the multitude.'
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Changes says that Meng nurtures through correctness, and that Mingyi governs the multitude through obscurity.

sentences.zh: 若其據尊極之位，衒聰耀明，恃才以肆，則上下不通，君臣道乖。

translations.literal: If one occupies the supreme position, displays cleverness and shines brilliance, relies on talent and acts arbitrarily, then above and below do not communicate and the way of ruler and minister is sundered.
translations.idiomatic: If one sits in the highest place, flaunts cleverness, dazzles with brilliance, and indulges talent in willful action, then communication between high and low breaks down and the bond between ruler and minister is severed.

sentences.zh: 自古滅亡，莫不由此。」

translations.literal: Since ancient times, extinction and ruin have never been otherwise."
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity onward, states have perished for no other reason."

sentences.zh: 帝稱善。

translations.literal: The emperor praised this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his answer.

sentences.zh: 除國子司業，歲餘，以太子右庶子兼司業。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Director of the Directorate of Education; after more than a year he additionally served as Right Vice Director of the Crown Prince while retaining the vice directorship.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Vice Director of the Directorate of Education, and a year later also served as Right Vice Director of the Crown Prince while keeping the vice directorship.

sentences.zh: 與諸儒議歷及明堂事，多從其說。

translations.literal: Together with the Confucians he debated the calendar and the Bright Hall; many followed his views.
translations.idiomatic: Debating the calendar and the Bright Hall with the Confucians, he won many over to his views.

sentences.zh: 以論撰勞，加散騎常侍，爵為子。

translations.literal: For the labor of compilation he was additionally appointed Regular Attendant and advanced in rank to Viscount.
translations.idiomatic: Rewarded for his work on the compilation, he was further made Regular Attendant and raised to the rank of Viscount.

sentences.zh: 皇太子令穎達撰《孝經章句》，因文以盡箴諷。

translations.literal: The crown prince ordered Yingda to compile Exegesis on the Classic of Filial Piety, using the text to exhaust admonition.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince ordered Yingda to compile an exegesis of the Classic of Filial Piety, drawing on the text to press every admonition home.

sentences.zh: 帝知數爭太子失，賜黃金一斤、絹百匹。

translations.literal: The emperor knew he repeatedly remonstrated with the crown prince over faults and bestowed one catty of gold and one hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing that Yingda had repeatedly corrected the crown prince's faults, the emperor bestowed one catty of gold and one hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 久之，拜祭酒，侍講東宮。

translations.literal: After a long time he was appointed Libationer and lectured in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was appointed Libationer and lectured in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 帝幸太學觀釋菜，命穎達講經，畢，上《釋奠頌》，有詔褒美。

translations.literal: When the emperor visited the Imperial University to observe the ceremonial offering, he ordered Yingda to expound the classics; when finished, Yingda submitted a Eulogy for the Ceremonial Offering, and an edict praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor visited the Imperial University for the ceremonial offering, he had Yingda expound the classics. When Yingda finished, he submitted a Eulogy for the Ceremonial Offering, and the court praised him by edict.

sentences.zh: 後太子稍不法，穎達爭不已，乳夫人曰：「太子既長，不宜數面折之。」

translations.literal: Later the crown prince gradually became improper in conduct; Yingda remonstrated without cease. The wet nurse said: "The crown prince has already grown; he should not be repeatedly rebuked to his face."
translations.idiomatic: Later, as the crown prince's conduct grew worse, Yingda remonstrated without cease. The wet nurse said, "The crown prince is grown now; he should not be corrected to his face again and again."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「蒙國厚恩，雖死不恨。」

translations.literal: He replied: "I have received the state's deep grace; though I die I have no regret."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "I owe the state a great debt; even if I die, I have no regret."

sentences.zh: 剴切愈至。

translations.literal: His earnestness became ever more severe.
translations.idiomatic: His remonstrances grew only more urgent.

sentences.zh: 後致仕，卒，陪葬昭陵，贈太常卿，謚曰憲。

translations.literal: Later he retired from office, died, was buried with honor at Zhaoling, was posthumously appointed Minister of Ceremonies, and given the posthumous title Xian.
translations.idiomatic: He later retired, died, and was buried with honor at Zhaoling; posthumously he was made Minister of Ceremonies and given the posthumous title Xian.

sentences.zh: 初，穎達與顏師古、司馬才章、王恭、王琰受詔撰《五經》義訓凡百餘篇，號《義贊》，詔改為《正義》雲。

translations.literal: At first Yingda together with Yan Shigu, Sima Caizhang, Wang Gong, and Wang Yan received orders to compile exegesis on the Five Classics totaling more than one hundred chapters, titled Yizan; an edict changed it to Zhengyi.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yingda had joined Yan Shigu, Sima Caizhang, Wang Gong, and Wang Yan in compiling more than one hundred chapters of exegesis on the Five Classics under the title Yizan; an edict renamed the work Zhengyi.

sentences.zh: 雖包貫異家為詳博，然其中不能無謬冗，博士馬嘉運駁正其失，至相譏詆。

translations.literal: Though it encompassed divergent schools and was detailed and broad, within it there could not but be errors and redundancy; Erudite Ma Jiayun refuted and corrected its faults, to the point of mutual ridicule and slander.
translations.idiomatic: Although the work embraced many schools and was exhaustive, it could not avoid error and redundancy; Erudite Ma Jiayun attacked its mistakes, and the two sides exchanged ridicule and slander.

sentences.zh: 有詔更令裁定，功未就。

translations.literal: An edict again ordered it to be examined and fixed; the work was not completed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered another round of revision, but the task was never finished.

sentences.zh: 永徽二年，詔中書門下與國子三館博士、弘文館學士考正之，於是尚書左僕射於誌寧、右僕射張行成、侍中高季輔就加增損，書始布下。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yonghui, the Secretariat and Chancellery together with erudites of the three academies of the Directorate of Education and academicians of the Hongwen Hall examined and corrected it; thereupon Left Vice Minister of Works Yu Zhining, Right Vice Minister Zhang Xingcheng, and Attendant Gao Jifu added and subtracted, and the book was finally promulgated.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yonghui, the Secretariat and Chancellery, together with erudites of the three academies and Hongwen academicians, reviewed the text. Left Vice Minister Yu Zhining, Right Vice Minister Zhang Xingcheng, and Attendant Gao Jifu then revised it further, and the book was finally issued.

sentences.zh: 穎達子誌，終司業。

translations.literal: Yingda's son Zhi ended as Vice Director of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Yingda's son Zhi eventually became Vice Director of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 誌子惠元，力學寡言，又為司業，擢累太子諭德。

translations.literal: Zhi's son Huiyuan, diligent in learning and sparing of speech, also became Vice Director, was repeatedly promoted, and ended as Preceptor of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi's son Huiyuan, a diligent scholar of few words, also rose to Vice Director and, after further promotion, ended as Preceptor of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 三世司業，時人美之。

translations.literal: Three generations as vice directors—men of the time praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Three generations in succession held the vice directorship, and contemporaries praised the family for it.

sentences.zh: 王恭者，滑州白馬人。

translations.literal: Wang Gong was a native of Baima in Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gong came from Baima in Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 少篤學，教授鄉閭，弟子數百人。

translations.literal: From youth he was deeply devoted to learning, teaching in his native district; his disciples numbered several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he devoted himself to learning and taught in his home district, gathering several hundred disciples.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，召拜太學博士，講《三禮》，別為《義證》，甚精博。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan he was summoned and appointed Erudite of the Imperial University, expounding the Three Rites; he separately compiled Yizheng, which was very precise and broad.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhenguan he was summoned as Erudite of the Imperial University and lectured on the Three Rites; he also compiled Yizheng, a work of great precision and breadth.

sentences.zh: 蓋文懿、文達皆當時大儒，每講遍舉先儒義，而必暢恭所說。

translations.literal: Gai Wenda and Wenda were great Confucians of the time; whenever they lectured they comprehensively cited earlier Confucians' meanings, yet always fully expounded Gong's explanations.
translations.idiomatic: Gai Wenda and Wenda were leading Confucians of the age; in lecturing they would survey earlier interpretations, yet always gave fullest weight to Gong's explanations.

sentences.zh: 馬嘉運，魏州繁水人。

translations.literal: Ma Jiayun was a native of Fanshui in Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Jiayun came from Fanshui in Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 少為沙門，還治儒學，長論議。

translations.literal: In youth he was a Buddhist monk; he returned to pursue Confucian learning and was skilled in debate.
translations.idiomatic: He had been a Buddhist monk in youth, then returned to Confucian study and became a formidable debater.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，累除越王東閣祭酒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan he was repeatedly removed and appointed Libationer of the Eastern Pavilion of the Prince of Yue.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhenguan he was repeatedly promoted and appointed Libationer of the Eastern Pavilion of the Prince of Yue.

sentences.zh: 退隱白鹿山，諸方來授業至千人。

translations.literal: He retired and hid on Mount Bailu; scholars came from all quarters to receive instruction, reaching a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He retired to Mount Bailu, where scholars came from every quarter to study under him until their number reached a thousand.

sentences.zh: 十一年，召拜太學博士、弘文館學士。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was summoned and appointed Erudite of the Imperial University and academician of the Hongwen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was recalled and made Erudite of the Imperial University and academician of the Hongwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 以孔穎達《正義》繁釀，故掎摭其疵，當世諸儒服其精。

translations.literal: Because Kong Yingda's Zhengyi was verbose and redundant, he picked out its flaws; Confucians of the age submitted to his precision.
translations.idiomatic: Finding Kong Yingda's Zhengyi wordy and overgrown, he exposed its flaws, and scholars of the age bowed to his exactness.

sentences.zh: 高宗為太子，引為崇賢館學士，數與洗馬秦暐侍講宮中，終國子博士。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong was crown prince, he was recruited as academician of the Chongxian Hall and often lectured in the palace together with Palace Steward Qin Hui; he ended as Erudite of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong was still crown prince, he was recruited to the Chongxian Hall and often lectured in the palace with Palace Steward Qin Hui; he ended his career as Erudite of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 詢初仿王羲之書，後險勁過之，因自名其體。

translations.literal: Xun at first imitated Wang Xizhi's calligraphy; later his sharp vigor surpassed it, and he thereby named his own style.
translations.idiomatic: Xun began by imitating Wang Xizhi's calligraphy, but later his sharp, forceful hand surpassed the model, and he gave his style its own name.

sentences.zh: 尺牘所傳，人以為法。

translations.literal: Letters transmitted on foot-long slips—people took them as the standard.
translations.idiomatic: The letters he wrote on foot-long slips became the standard others followed.

sentences.zh: 高麗嘗遣使求之，帝嘆曰：「彼觀其書，固謂形貌魁梧邪？」

translations.literal: Goguryeo once sent envoys to request them; the emperor sighed and said: "When they see his writing, do they indeed think his form and appearance are towering?"
translations.idiomatic: When Goguryeo once sent envoys to request samples, the emperor sighed and said, "When they see his writing, do they imagine his person is equally towering?"

sentences.zh: 嘗行見索靖所書碑，觀之，去數步復返，及疲，乃布坐，至宿其傍，三日乃得去。

translations.literal: Once on the road he saw a stele inscribed by Suo Jing; he viewed it, went several paces away and returned, and when exhausted spread a mat and sat; he stayed by it three days before he could leave.
translations.idiomatic: Once on the road he came upon a stele inscribed by Suo Jing. He studied it, walked away, returned, and when exhausted spread a mat beside it; he remained there three days before he could tear himself away.

sentences.zh: 其所嗜類此。

translations.literal: What he loved was of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His passions ran to such things.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，歷太子率更令、弘文館學士，封渤海男。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan he successively served as Director of the Crown Prince's Rate Bureau and academician of the Hongwen Hall, and was enfeoffed as Baron of Bohai.
