translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhenguan he served successively as Director of the Crown Prince's Rate Bureau and Hongwen academician, and was enfeoffed as Baron of Bohai.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十五。

translations.literal: He died at the age of eighty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty-five.

sentences.zh: 子通，儀鳳中累遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: His son Tong, in the Yifeng era was repeatedly promoted to Secretariat Draftsman.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tong rose during the Yifeng era to Secretariat Draftsman.

sentences.zh: 居母喪，詔奪哀。

translations.literal: When in mourning for his mother, an edict ordered mourning cut short.
translations.idiomatic: While mourning his mother, he was ordered by edict to cut short his mourning.

sentences.zh: 每入朝，徒跣及門。

translations.literal: Each time he entered court he went barefoot to the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he entered court he went barefoot as far as the gate.

sentences.zh: 夜直，藉槁以寢。

translations.literal: On night duty he slept on straw.
translations.idiomatic: On night duty he slept on straw bedding.

sentences.zh: 非公事不語，還家輒號慟。

translations.literal: He spoke only on public affairs; returning home he always wailed aloud.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke only on public business; at home he wailed aloud without cease.

sentences.zh: 年饑，未克葬，居廬四年，不釋服。

translations.literal: In a year of famine he could not yet bury her; he dwelt in the mourning hut four years without removing mourning garments.
translations.idiomatic: During a famine year he could not yet bury her; he lived in the mourning hut four years without putting off mourning dress.

sentences.zh: 冬月，家人以氈絮潛置席下，通覺，即徹去。

translations.literal: In winter his family secretly placed felt padding under his mat; Tong noticed and immediately removed it.
translations.idiomatic: In winter his family secretly placed felt under his mat; Tong noticed at once and had it removed.

sentences.zh: 遷累殿中監，封渤海子。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Director of the Palace Bureau and enfeoffed as Viscount of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to Director of the Palace Bureau and enfeoffed as Viscount of Bohai.

sentences.zh: 天授初，轉司禮卿，判納言事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianshou he was transferred to Minister of Ceremonies and concurrently judged affairs of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianshou he became Minister of Ceremonies and concurrently handled Censorate affairs.

sentences.zh: 輔政月餘，會鳳閣舍人張嘉福請以武承嗣為太子，通與岑長倩等固執，忤諸武意。

translations.literal: Assisting in government for more than a month, when Phoenix Pavilion Draftsman Zhang Jiafu requested that Wu Chengsi be made crown prince, Tong together with Cen Changqian and others firmly resisted, offending the Wu clan.
translations.idiomatic: After little more than a month assisting the government, when Phoenix Pavilion Draftsman Zhang Jiafu proposed making Wu Chengsi crown prince, Tong joined Cen Changqian and others in firm opposition, offending the Wu clan.

sentences.zh: 及長倩下獄，坐大逆死，來俊臣並引通同謀，通雖被慘毒無異詞，俊臣代占，誅之。

translations.literal: When Changqian was imprisoned, Tong was charged with great treason and executed; Lai Junchen also implicated Tong in the same plot; though Tong suffered cruel torture he did not change his words, and Junchen forged his confession and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Changqian was imprisoned, Tong was charged with treason and executed. Lai Junchen implicated him in the same plot; though Tong endured cruel torture without changing his words, Junchen forged a confession and had him killed.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，追復官爵。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong his office and rank were posthumously restored.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Shenlong his offices and rank were posthumously restored.

sentences.zh: 通蚤孤，母徐教以父書，懼其墮，嘗遺錢使市父遺跡，通乃刻意臨仿以求售，數年，書亞於詢，父子齊名，號「大小歐陽體」。

translations.literal: Tong lost his father early; his mother Xu taught him his father's calligraphy, fearing he would decline; she once gave him money to buy his father's surviving works; Tong then deliberately copied them to sell; within several years his writing was second only to Xun's; father and son were equally renowned, styled the "Large and Small Ouyang Styles."
translations.idiomatic: Tong lost his father early. His mother Xu taught him his father's calligraphy, fearing his skill would slip; she once gave him money to buy his father's surviving pieces, and Tong deliberately copied them for sale. Within a few years his writing ranked just below Xun's; father and son became equally famous as the "Large and Small Ouyang Styles."

sentences.zh: 褚遂良亦以書自名，嘗問虞世南曰：「吾書何如智永？」

translations.literal: Chu Suiliang also made a name for himself in calligraphy; he once asked Yu Shinan: "How is my writing compared with Zhiyong's?"
translations.idiomatic: Chu Suiliang also won fame in calligraphy. He once asked Yu Shinan, "How does my writing compare with Zhiyong's?"

sentences.zh: 答曰：「吾聞彼一字直五萬，君豈得此？」

translations.literal: He replied: "I hear one character of his is worth fifty thousand; can you obtain this?"
translations.idiomatic: Shinan replied, "I hear one character of his is worth fifty thousand cash—can you match that?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「孰與詢？」

translations.literal: He said: "Compared with Xun?"
translations.idiomatic: Suiliang asked, "And compared with Xun?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「吾聞詢不擇紙筆，皆得如誌，君豈得此？」

translations.literal: He said: "I hear Xun, regardless of paper or brush, all come out like his intent; can you obtain this?"
translations.idiomatic: Shinan said, "I hear Xun, whatever the paper or brush, always produces what he intends—can you do that?"

sentences.zh: 遂良曰：「然則何如？」

translations.literal: Suiliang said: "Then how is it?"
translations.idiomatic: Suiliang said, "Then where do I stand?"

sentences.zh: 世南曰：「君若手和筆調，固可貴尚。」

translations.literal: Shinan said: "If your hand harmonizes and brush is tuned, it can indeed be honored."
translations.idiomatic: Shinan said, "If hand and brush are in harmony, your work can indeed be admired."

sentences.zh: 遂良大喜。

translations.literal: Suiliang greatly rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Suiliang was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 通晚自矜重，以貍毛為筆，覆以兔毫，管皆象犀，非是未嘗書。

translations.literal: In his later years Tong prided himself and was self-restrained; he used raccoon fur for the brush and covered it with rabbit hair; the tube was all ivory and rhinoceros horn—unless it was such he never wrote.
translations.idiomatic: In later years Tong grew proud and exacting: he used raccoon fur for the brush core, covered it with rabbit hair, and would write only with tubes of ivory and rhinoceros horn.

sentences.zh: 朱子奢，蘇州吳人，從鄉人顧彪授《左氏春秋》，善文辭。

translations.literal: Zhu Zishe was a native of Wu in Suzhou; he studied the Zuo clan Spring and Autumn Annals under Gu Biao of his district and was skilled in literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Zishe, a native of Wu in Suzhou, studied the Zuo clan Spring and Autumn Annals under Gu Biao and was skilled in prose.

sentences.zh: 隋大業中，為直秘書學士。

translations.literal: In the Daye era of Sui he served as Direct Secretariat Academician.
translations.idiomatic: During Sui's Daye era he served as Direct Secretariat Academician.

sentences.zh: 天下亂，辭疾還鄉里。

translations.literal: When the realm fell into disorder he pleaded illness and returned to his native place.
translations.idiomatic: When the realm fell into chaos he pleaded illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 後從杜伏威入朝，授國子助教。

translations.literal: Later he followed Du Fuwei into court and was appointed Assistant Instructor of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He later followed Du Fuwei to court and was appointed Assistant Instructor of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 太宗貞觀初，高麗、百濟同伐新羅，連年兵不解。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan of Emperor Taizong, Goguryeo and Baekje together attacked Silla; warfare continued for years without resolution.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Taizong's Zhenguan reign, Goguryeo and Baekje jointly attacked Silla, and war dragged on for years without resolution.

sentences.zh: 新羅告急，帝假子奢員外散騎侍郎，持節諭旨，平三國之憾。

translations.literal: Silla reported urgency; the emperor temporarily appointed Zishe Outer Office Member of the Secretariat with credentials to convey the imperial intent and settle the grievances of the three states.
translations.idiomatic: When Silla sent urgent appeals, the emperor temporarily appointed Zishe Outer Office Member of the Secretariat with credentials to convey the imperial will and settle the quarrel among the three kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 子奢有儀觀，夷人尊畏之。

translations.literal: Zishe had dignified bearing; the barbarians honored and feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Zishe had a commanding presence, and the foreign rulers both honored and feared him.

sentences.zh: 二國上書謝罪，贈遺甚厚。

translations.literal: The two states submitted letters of apology; their gifts were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: Both states sent letters of apology and offered lavish gifts.

sentences.zh: 初，子奢行，帝戒曰：「海夷重學，卿為講大誼，然勿入其幣，還當以中書舍人處卿。」

translations.literal: At first when Zishe departed, the emperor admonished him: "The maritime barbarians value learning; you will expound the great meaning for them—but do not accept their gifts; on return you will be placed as Secretariat Draftsman."
translations.idiomatic: Before Zishe departed, the emperor warned him: "The maritime peoples respect learning; expound the great principles to them—but do not accept their gifts. On your return I shall appoint you Secretariat Draftsman."

sentences.zh: 子奢唯唯。

translations.literal: Zishe assented repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: Zishe agreed again and again.

sentences.zh: 至其國，為發《春秋》題，納其美女。

translations.literal: Arriving in their countries, he issued Spring and Autumn questions and accepted their beautiful women.
translations.idiomatic: Once in their lands he set Spring and Autumn questions—and accepted their beautiful women.

sentences.zh: 帝責違旨，而猶愛其才，以散官直國子學，累轉諫議大夫、弘文館學士。

translations.literal: The emperor reproached him for violating the instruction, yet still cherished his talent; he was made unattached official on duty at the Directorate of Education and was repeatedly transferred to Remonstrator of the Left and academician of the Hongwen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked him for disobeying orders, yet still valued his talent; he was kept as an unattached official at the Directorate of Education and later rose to Remonstrator of the Left and Hongwen academician.

sentences.zh: 始，武德時，太廟享止四室，高祖崩，將祔主於廟，帝詔有司詳議。

translations.literal: At first, in the Wude era, the Imperial Ancestral Temple sacrifices stopped at four chambers; when Emperor Gaozu died and his tablet was to be enshrined in the temple, the emperor ordered the relevant offices to discuss in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the Wude era, sacrifices at the Imperial Ancestral Temple were limited to four chambers. When Emperor Gaozu died and his tablet was to be installed, the emperor ordered a full deliberation.

sentences.zh: 子奢建言：「漢丞相韋玄成奏立五廟，劉歆議當七，鄭玄本玄成，王肅宗歆，於是歷代廟議不能一。

translations.literal: Zishe proposed: "Han Chancellor Wei Xuancheng memorialized establishing five temples; Liu Xin debated that it should be seven; Zheng Xuan followed Xuancheng, Wang Su followed Liu Xin—thus through the ages temple debate could not be one.
translations.idiomatic: Zishe argued: "Han Chancellor Wei Xuancheng proposed five temples; Liu Xin argued for seven; Zheng Xuan followed Xuancheng, Wang Su followed Liu Xin—so temple practice has never been settled.

sentences.zh: 且天子七廟，諸侯五，降殺以兩，禮之正也。

translations.literal: Moreover the Son of Heaven has seven temples, feudal lords five—the descent by two ranks is the correct rite.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Son of Heaven keeps seven temples and feudal lords five; the step down by two ranks is the proper rite.

sentences.zh: 若天子與子、男同，則間無容等，非德厚遊廣、德薄遊狹之義。

translations.literal: If the Son of Heaven is the same as viscounts and barons, then between ranks there is no room for gradation—this is not the meaning of greater virtue traveling broadly and lesser virtue traveling narrowly.
translations.idiomatic: If the Son of Heaven were no different from viscounts and barons, there would be no gradation between ranks—contrary to the principle that greater virtue ranges widely and lesser virtue more narrowly.

sentences.zh: 臣請依古為七廟。

translations.literal: Your subject requests following antiquity in establishing seven temples.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject asks that seven temples be established according to antiquity.

sentences.zh: 若親盡，則以王業所基為太祖，虛太祖室以俟無疆，叠遷乃處之。」

translations.literal: When kin is exhausted, then take the founder of the royal enterprise as Grand Ancestor and leave the Grand Ancestor chamber empty awaiting the boundless future; when tablets are shifted in succession they are then placed there."
translations.idiomatic: When the line of kin is exhausted, the founder of the royal enterprise should become Grand Ancestor, with the Grand Ancestor chamber left empty for the boundless future; tablets are moved there in succession as the line advances."

sentences.zh: 於是尚書共奏：「自《春秋》以來，言天子七廟，諸侯五，大夫三，士二。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Ministry of Works jointly memorialized: "Since the Spring and Autumn Annals, it is said the Son of Heaven has seven temples, feudal lords five, grand masters three, and officers two.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Works then jointly memorialized: "Since the Spring and Autumn Annals, tradition holds that the Son of Heaven has seven temples, feudal lords five, grand masters three, and officers two.

sentences.zh: 推親親，顯尊尊，為不可易之法，請建親廟六。」

translations.literal: Extending kinship and displaying honor of the honored is an unchangeable law; we request establishing six kin temples."
translations.idiomatic: Extending kinship and displaying the honor due the honored is an unchanging law; we ask that six kin temples be established."

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved.

sentences.zh: 乃祔弘農府君、高祖神主為六室。

translations.literal: Thereupon the tablets of Lord of Hongnong and Emperor Gaozu were enshrined as six chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the tablets of Lord of Hongnong and Emperor Gaozu were installed as six chambers.

sentences.zh: 及帝崩，禮部尚書許敬宗議：「弘農府君廟應毀。

translations.literal: When the emperor died, Minister of Rites Xu Jingzong debated: "The temple of Lord of Hongnong should be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died, Minister of Rites Xu Jingzong argued that the temple of Lord of Hongnong should be abolished.

sentences.zh: 按玄成說，毀廟主當瘞，且四海常所宗享矣，舉而瘞之，非神理所愜。

translations.literal: According to Xuancheng's view, when destroying a temple tablet it should be buried; yet the four seas constantly offer sacrifice to it—raising it and burying it does not satisfy divine principle.
translations.idiomatic: By Xuancheng's view, a destroyed tablet should be buried; yet the realm still sacrifices to it—to remove and bury it would violate divine principle.

sentences.zh: 晉範宣議別廟以奉毀廟之主，或言當藏天府。

translations.literal: Fan Xuan of Jin debated establishing a separate temple to serve destroyed temple tablets; some said they should be stored in the Heavenly Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Xuan of Jin proposed a separate temple for removed tablets; others said they should be kept in the Heavenly Storehouse.

sentences.zh: 天府，瑞異所舍也。

translations.literal: The Heavenly Storehouse is where auspicious anomalies are kept.
translations.idiomatic: The Heavenly Storehouse is where portents and anomalies are stored.

sentences.zh: 《禮》去祧有壇有墠，臣皆所未安。

translations.literal: The Rites say for removed tablets there are altars and open spaces—I am not yet at ease with any of these.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites prescribe altars and open spaces for removed tablets—I am satisfied with none of these options.

sentences.zh: 唐家宗廟，共殿異室，以右為首。

translations.literal: Tang ancestral temples share halls but have separate chambers, with the right as chief.
translations.idiomatic: Tang ancestral temples share a hall but have separate chambers, with the right side chief.

sentences.zh: 若奉遷主納右夾室，而得尊處，祈之禱之未絕也。」

translations.literal: If removed tablets are placed in the right side chamber and thereby receive honored placement, prayer to them has not ceased."
translations.idiomatic: If removed tablets are placed in the right side chamber and thus retain honored standing, prayers to them need not cease."

sentences.zh: 有詔如敬宗議。

translations.literal: An edict followed Jingzong's debate.
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed Jingzong's proposal.

sentences.zh: 然言七廟者，本之子奢。

translations.literal: Yet those who spoke of seven temples originated with Zishe.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the argument for seven temples had originated with Zishe.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗詔：「起居紀錄臧否，朕欲見之以知得失，若何？」

translations.literal: The emperor once ordered: "The records of rise and fall note praise and blame; I wish to see them to know gain and loss—what of it?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once asked, "The records of rise and fall note praise and blame; I wish to read them to know my gains and losses—what harm is there?"

sentences.zh: 子奢曰：「陛下所舉無過事，雖見無嫌，然以此開後世史官之禍，可懼也。

translations.literal: Zishe said: "Your Majesty's actions have no excess; though you see them there is no offense—yet to open this door for later generations' historiographers is to be feared.
translations.idiomatic: Zishe replied, "Your Majesty's conduct is without excess, and there would be no shame in reading the records—but to open this door for later historiographers is dangerous.

sentences.zh: 史官全身畏死，則悠悠千載，尚有聞乎？」

translations.literal: Historiographers preserving themselves fear death; then for a thousand years will anything still be heard?"
translations.idiomatic: If historiographers must preserve themselves and fear death, then after a thousand years will anything truthful still be heard?"

sentences.zh: 池陽令崔文康坐事，櫟陽尉魏禮臣劾治，獄成，御史言其枉。

translations.literal: Magistrate Cui Wenkang of Chiyang was charged with an offense; Assistant Magistrate Wei Lichen investigated and the case was complete; the censor said he was wronged.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Cui Wenkang of Chiyang was charged with an offense; Assistant Magistrate Wei Lichen completed the investigation, but the censor declared the verdict unjust.

sentences.zh: 禮臣訴御史阿黨，乞下有司雜訊，不如所言請死。

translations.literal: Lichen appealed that the censor showed factional favor and requested handing down to the relevant offices for mixed interrogation; if not as he said he requested death.
translations.idiomatic: Lichen appealed that the censor had shown factional favor and asked that the case be sent to the relevant offices for joint interrogation, offering his own life if his claim proved false.

sentences.zh: 鞫報禮臣不實，詔如請。

translations.literal: The interrogation reported Lichen's claim was not true; an edict followed his request.
translations.idiomatic: The interrogation reported Lichen's claim was not true, an edict followed his request.

sentences.zh: 子奢曰：「在律，上書不實有定罪，今抵以死，死者不可復生，雖欲自新弗可得。

translations.literal: Zishe said: "In law, submitting a memorial that is not true has a fixed punishment; now to punish with death—the dead cannot be revived; though one wishes to reform oneself it cannot be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Zishe said: "In law, submitting a memorial that is not true has a fixed punishment, now to punish with death—the dead cannot be revived, though one wishes to reform oneself it cannot be obtained.

sentences.zh: 且天下惟知上書獲罪，欲自言者，皆懼而不敢申矣。」

translations.literal: Moreover all under Heaven will know only that submitting memorials brings punishment; those who wish to speak will all fear and dare not report."
translations.idiomatic: Furthermore, all under Heaven will know only that submitting memorials brings punishment; those who wish to speak will all fear and dare not report."

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved.

sentences.zh: 子奢為人樂易，能劇談，以經誼緣飾。

translations.literal: Zishe as a man was easygoing, could debate vigorously, and adorned matters with classical meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Zishe as a man was easygoing. could debate vigorously, and adorned matters with classical meaning.

sentences.zh: 每侍宴，帝令論難群臣，恩禮甚篤。

translations.literal: Whenever he attended banquets the emperor ordered him to debate with ministers; grace and ceremony were very thick.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he attended banquets the emperor ordered him to debate with ministers, grace and ceremony were very thick.

sentences.zh: 卒於官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 張士衡，瀛州樂壽人。

translations.literal: Zhang Shiheng was a native of Leshou in Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shiheng came from Leshou in Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 父文慶，北齊國子助教。

translations.literal: His father Wenqing was Erudite of the Directorate of Education of Northern Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His father, Wenqing was Erudite of the Directorate of Education of Northern Qi.

sentences.zh: 士衡九歲居母喪，哀慕過禮。

translations.literal: Shiheng at nine was in mourning for his mother; his grief exceeded the rites.
translations.idiomatic: Shiheng at nine was in mourning for his mother, his grief exceeded the rites.

sentences.zh: 博士劉軌思見之，為泣下，奇其操，謂文慶曰：「古不親教子，吾為君成就之。」

translations.literal: Erudite Liu Guisi saw this and wept for him, marveling at his conduct, and said to Wenqing: "In antiquity fathers did not personally teach sons; I will complete him for you."
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Liu Guisi saw this and wept for him, marveling at his conduct, and said to Wenqing: "In antiquity fathers did not personally teach sons, I will complete him for you."

sentences.zh: 乃授以《詩》、《禮》。

translations.literal: Thereupon he instructed him in the Odes and Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He then instructed him in the Odes and Rites.

sentences.zh: 又從熊安生、劉焯等受經，貫知大義。

translations.literal: He also studied under Xiong Ansheng, Liu Zhuo, and others and thoroughly knew the great meaning.
translations.idiomatic: He also studied under Xiong Ansheng. Liu Zhuo, and others and thoroughly knew the great meaning.

sentences.zh: 仕隋為餘杭令，以老還家。

translations.literal: Serving Sui as Magistrate of Yuhang, he returned home in old age.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sui he served as Magistrate of Yuhang, then returned home in old age.

sentences.zh: 大業兵起，諸儒廢學。

translations.literal: When Daye warfare arose, the Confucians abandoned study.
translations.idiomatic: When Daye warfare arose. the Confucians abandoned study.

sentences.zh: 唐興，士衡復講教鄉里。

translations.literal: When Tang arose, Shiheng again taught in his native district.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang arose. Shiheng again taught in his native district.

sentences.zh: 幽州都督燕王靈夔以禮邀聘，北面事之。

translations.literal: Regional Inspector Ling Cai of Youzhou invited him with ceremony; he served him facing north.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Inspector Ling Cai of Youzhou invited him with ceremony, he served him facing north.

sentences.zh: 太子承乾慕風迎致，謁太宗洛陽宮，帝賜食，擢朝散大夫、崇賢館學士。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Chengqian, admiring his reputation, welcomed and brought him; he had an audience at Luoyang Palace of Emperor Taizong; the emperor bestowed food and promoted him to Grand Master of the Palace and academician of the Chongxian Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Chengqian, admiring his reputation, welcomed and brought him, he had an audience at Luoyang Palace of Emperor Taizong, the emperor bestowed food and promoted him to Grand Master of the Palace and academician of the Chongxian Hall.

sentences.zh: 太子以士衡齊人也，問高氏何以亡？

translations.literal: The crown prince, because Shiheng was a man of Qi, asked why the Gao house perished.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince. because Shiheng was a man of Qi, asked why the Gao house perished.

sentences.zh: 士衡曰：「高阿那瑰之兇險，駱提婆之佞，韓長鸞之虐，皆奴隸才，是信是使，忠良外誅，骨肉內離，剝喪黎元，故周師臨郊，人莫為之用，此所以亡。」

translations.literal: Shiheng said: "Gao Anaguli's viciousness, Luo Tipo's flattery, Han Changluan's cruelty—all were talents of slaves, trusted and employed; loyal men were executed outside, flesh and blood divided within; they stripped and harmed the people—therefore when Zhou armies reached the suburbs no one would act for them; this is why they perished."
translations.idiomatic: Shiheng said: "Gao Anaguli's viciousness, Luo Tipo's flattery, Han Changluan's cruelty—all were talents of slaves, trusted and employed, loyal men were executed outside, flesh and blood divided within, they stripped and harmed the people—therefore when Zhou armies reached the suburbs no one would act for them, this is why they perished."

sentences.zh: 復問：「事佛營福，其應奈何？」

translations.literal: He again asked: "Serving Buddha to seek blessing—what is the response?"
translations.idiomatic: He again asked: "Serving Buddha to seek blessing—what is the response?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「事佛在清靜仁恕爾，如貪婪驕虐，雖傾財事之，無損於禍。

translations.literal: He replied: "Serving Buddha lies in purity, quiet, benevolence, and forgiveness; if greedy, arrogant, and cruel, though one exhausts wealth in serving it, it does not lessen disaster.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Serving Buddha lies in purity, quiet, benevolence, and forgiveness; if greedy, arrogant, and cruel, though one exhausts wealth in serving it, it does not lessen disaster.

sentences.zh: 且善惡必報，若影赴形，聖人言之備矣。

translations.literal: Moreover good and evil must be requited, like shadow following form—the sage spoke of this completely.
translations.idiomatic: Furthermore, good and evil must be requited, like shadow following form—the sage spoke of this completely.

sentences.zh: 為君仁，為臣忠，為子孝，則福祚永；

translations.literal: If the ruler is benevolent, the minister loyal, the son filial, then fortune and rank endure;
translations.idiomatic: If the ruler is benevolent. the minister loyal, the son filial, then fortune and rank endure;

sentences.zh: 反是而殃禍至矣！」

translations.literal: reverse this and calamity arrives!"
translations.idiomatic: turn these virtues upside down and calamity follows!"

sentences.zh: 時太子以過失聞，士衡因是規之，然不能用也。

translations.literal: At the time the crown prince's faults were heard of; Shiheng thereby admonished him, yet he could not be employed.
translations.idiomatic: While the time the crown prince's faults were heard of; Shiheng thereby admonished him, yet he could not be employed.

sentences.zh: 太子廢，給傳罷歸鄉里，卒。

translations.literal: When the crown prince was deposed, he was given post horses and dismissed to his native district; he died.
translations.idiomatic: After the crown prince was deposed, he was given post horses and dismissed to his native district; he died.

sentences.zh: 士衡以《禮》教諸生，當時顯者：永平賈公彥、趙李玄植。

translations.literal: Shiheng taught the Rites to students; at the time the prominent were Jia Gongyan of Yongping and Li Xuanzhi of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Shiheng taught the Rites to students, at the time the prominent were Jia Gongyan of Yongping and Li Xuanzhi of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 公彥終太學博士，撰次章句甚多。

translations.literal: Gongyan ended as Erudite of the Imperial University and compiled many chapters of exegesis.
translations.idiomatic: Gongyan finished as Erudite of the Imperial University and compiled many chapters of exegesis.

sentences.zh: 子大隱，儀鳳中，為太常博士。

translations.literal: His son Dayin, in the Yifeng era, was Erudite of the Ministry of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: His son Dayin. in the Yifeng era, was Erudite of the Ministry of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 會太常仲春告瑞太廟，高宗問禮官：「何世而然？」

translations.literal: When the Ministry of Ceremonies in mid-spring reported auspicious signs to the Grand Ancestral Temple, Emperor Gaozong asked the ritual officials: "From what age has this been so?"
translations.idiomatic: When the Ministry of Ceremonies in mid-spring reported auspicious signs to the Grand Ancestral Temple, Emperor Gaozong asked the ritual officials: "From what age has this been so?"

sentences.zh: 大隱對曰：「古者祭以首時，薦以仲月。

translations.literal: Dayin replied: "In antiquity sacrifice was at the head of the season and offering at the middle month.
translations.idiomatic: Dayin replied: "In antiquity sacrifice became at the head of the season and offering at the middle month.

sentences.zh: 近世元日奏瑞，則二月告廟。

translations.literal: In recent ages on New Year's Day auspicious signs were reported, then in the second month the temple was notified.
translations.idiomatic: In recent ages on New Year's Day auspicious signs were reported, then in the second month the temple became notified.

sentences.zh: 告者必有薦，本於始不得其時焉。」

translations.literal: Reporting necessarily has offering—this originates in not obtaining the proper season at the start."
translations.idiomatic: Reporting necessarily has offering—this originates in not obtaining the proper season at the start."

sentences.zh: 遷累中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Secretariat Draftsman.
translations.idiomatic: He became repeatedly promoted to Secretariat Draftsman.

sentences.zh: 垂拱中，博士周悰請武氏廟為七室，唐廟為五，下比諸侯。

translations.literal: In the Chuigong era, Erudite Zhou Cong requested the Wu clan temple have seven chambers and the Tang temple five, lowering it to compare with feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: In the Chuigong era. Erudite Zhou Cong requested the Wu clan temple have seven chambers and the Tang temple five, lowering it to compare with feudal lords.

sentences.zh: 大隱奏言：「秦、漢母後稱制，未有戾古越禮者。

translations.literal: Dayin memorialized: "Qin and Han empress dowagers who held regency never violated antiquity or exceeded rites.
translations.idiomatic: Dayin memorialized: "Qin and Han empress dowagers who held regency never violated antiquity or exceeded rites.

sentences.zh: 悰損國廟數，悖大義，不可以訓。」

translations.literal: Cong diminishes the number of state temples and violates great principle—it cannot serve as instruction."
translations.idiomatic: Cong diminishes the number of state temples and violates great principle—it cannot serve as instruction."

sentences.zh: 武後不獲已，偽聽之。

translations.literal: Empress Wu, unable to obtain her wish, pretended to assent.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu. unable to obtain her wish, pretended to assent.

sentences.zh: 時皆服大隱沈正不詭從，有大臣體。

translations.literal: At the time all submitted to Dayin's deep correctness and unwavering compliance—he had the bearing of a great minister.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, all submitted to Dayin's deep correctness and unwavering compliance—he had the bearing of a great minister.

sentences.zh: 終禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: He ended as Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He finished his career as Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 公彥傳業玄植，玄植又受《左氏春秋》於王德韶，受《詩》於齊威，該覽百家記書。

translations.literal: Gongyan transmitted the learning to Xuanzhi; Xuanzhi also received the Zuo clan Spring and Autumn Annals from Wang Deshao and the Odes from Qi Wei, and comprehensively read the records of the hundred schools.
translations.idiomatic: Gongyan transmitted the learning to Xuanzhi, Xuanzhi also received the Zuo clan Spring and Autumn Annals from Wang Deshao and the Odes from Qi Wei, and comprehensively read the records of the hundred schools.

sentences.zh: 貞觀間，為弘文館直學士。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan era he was Direct Academician of the Hongwen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguan era he was Direct Academician of the Hongwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 高宗時，數召見，與方士、浮屠講說。

translations.literal: In Emperor Gaozong's time he was repeatedly summoned and lectured together with Daoists and Buddhists.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Gaozong's time he became repeatedly summoned and lectured together with Daoists and Buddhists.

sentences.zh: 玄植以帝暗弱，頗箴切其短，帝禮之，不寤。

translations.literal: Xuanzhi, because the emperor was weak and dark, often admonished his faults sharply; the emperor treated him with ceremony but did not awaken.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzhi, because the emperor was weak and dark, often admonished his faults sharply, the emperor treated him with ceremony but did not awaken.

sentences.zh: 坐事遷巴令，卒。

translations.literal: Charged with an offense he was transferred to Magistrate of Ba and died.
translations.idiomatic: After being charged with an offense, he was transferred to Magistrate of Ba and died.

sentences.zh: 張後胤，字嗣宗，蘇州昆山人。

translations.literal: Zhang Houyin, styled Sizong, was a native of Kunshan in Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Houyin. styled Sizong, was a native of Kunshan in Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖僧紹，梁零陵太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Sengshao was Prefect of Lingling of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Sengshao became Prefect of Lingling of Liang.

sentences.zh: 父沖，陳國子博士，入隋為漢王諒并州博士。

translations.literal: His father Chong was Erudite of the Directorate of Education of Chen; entering Sui he became Erudite of the Prince of Han, Liang, in Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father, Chong was Erudite of the Directorate of Education of Chen; entering Sui he became Erudite of the Prince of Han, Liang, in Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 後胤甫冠，以學行禪其家。

translations.literal: Houyin had just reached adulthood and by learning and conduct surpassed his family.
translations.idiomatic: Houyin had just reached adulthood and by learning and conduct surpassed his family.

sentences.zh: 高祖鎮太原，引為客，以經授秦王。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu garrisoned Taiyuan he recruited him as a guest and had him instruct the Prince of Qin in the classics.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu garrisoned Taiyuan he recruited him as a guest and had him instruct the Prince of Qin in the classics.

sentences.zh: 義寧初，為齊王文學，封新野縣公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yining he was Literary Officer of the Prince of Qi and enfeoffed as Duke of Xinye.
translations.idiomatic: During the early Yining he was Literary Officer of the Prince of Qi and enfeoffed as Duke of Xinye.

sentences.zh: 武德中，擢員外散騎侍郎，賜宅一區。

translations.literal: In the Wude era he was promoted to Outer Office Member of the Regular Attendant and bestowed one residence.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wude era he was promoted to Outer Office Member of the Regular Attendant and bestowed one residence.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，進燕王諮議，從王入朝，召見。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong took the throne he was advanced to Adviser of the Prince of Yan and followed the prince into court; he was summoned for audience.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong took the throne he was advanced to Adviser of the Prince of Yan and followed the prince into court, he was summoned for audience.

sentences.zh: 初，帝在太原，嘗問：「隋運將終，得天下者何姓？」

translations.literal: At first when the emperor was at Taiyuan he once asked: "The Sui fortune is about to end—what surname will obtain all under Heaven?"
translations.idiomatic: At first when the emperor became at Taiyuan he once asked: "The Sui fortune is about to end—what surname will obtain all under Heaven?"

sentences.zh: 答曰：「公家德業，天下系心，若順天而動，自河以北，指撝可定。

translations.literal: He replied: "Your house's virtue and enterprise— all under Heaven fix their hearts on it; if you move according to Heaven, from north of the River you can settle things with a gesture.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Your house's virtue and enterprise— all under Heaven fix their hearts on it; if you move according to Heaven, from north of the River you can settle things with a gesture.

sentences.zh: 然後長驅關右，帝業可成。」

translations.literal: Then drive long through the passes west and the imperial enterprise can be achieved."
translations.idiomatic: Then drive long through the passes west and the imperial enterprise can be achieved."

sentences.zh: 至是自陳所言，帝曰：「是事未始忘之。」

translations.literal: Now he himself stated what he had said; the emperor said: "That matter I have never forgotten."
translations.idiomatic: At present, he himself stated what he had said; the emperor said: "That matter I have never forgotten."

sentences.zh: 乃賜燕月池。

translations.literal: Thereupon he bestowed the Yan Moon Pond.
translations.idiomatic: He then bestowed the Yan Moon Pond.

sentences.zh: 帝從容曰：「今日弟子何如？」

translations.literal: The emperor said at ease: "How is your disciple today?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then said at ease: "How is your disciple today?"

sentences.zh: 後胤曰：「昔孔子門人三千，達者無子男之位。

translations.literal: Houyin said: "Formerly Confucius had three thousand disciples; those who attained rank had none at viscount or baron.
translations.idiomatic: Houyin said: "Formerly Confucius had three thousand disciples, those who attained rank had none at viscount or baron.

sentences.zh: 臣翼贊一人，乃王天下，計臣之功，過於先聖。」

translations.literal: Your subject assisted one man who then ruled all under Heaven; counting your subject's achievement, it surpasses the former sage."
translations.idiomatic: Your subject assisted one man who then ruled all under Heaven, counting your subject's achievement, it surpasses the former sage."

sentences.zh: 帝為之笑，令群臣以《春秋》酬難。

translations.literal: The emperor laughed at this and ordered ministers to exchange challenges on the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed at this and ordered ministers to exchange challenges on the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕昔受大誼於君，今尚記之。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I formerly received the great meaning from you; I still remember it."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then said: "I formerly received the great meaning from you; I still remember it."

sentences.zh: 後胤頓首謝曰：「陛下乃生知，臣叨天功為己力，罪也。」

translations.literal: Houyin bowed his head and thanked him: "Your Majesty was born knowing; your subject presumptuously took Heaven's achievement as his own strength—this is a crime."
translations.idiomatic: Houyin bowed his head and thanked him: "Your Majesty was born knowing, your subject presumptuously took Heaven's achievement as his own strength—this is a crime."

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，遷燕王府司馬。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly rejoiced and transferred him to Administrative Assistant of the Princely Household of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor greatly rejoiced and transferred him to Administrative Assistant of the Princely Household of Yan.

sentences.zh: 出為睦州刺史，乞骸骨，帝見其強力，問欲何官，因陳謝不敢。

translations.literal: Going out as Prefect of Muzhou he requested retirement; the emperor, seeing his vigor, asked what office he wished; he declined and did not dare.
translations.idiomatic: Going out as Prefect of Muzhou he requested retirement, the emperor, seeing his vigor, asked what office he wished, he declined and did not dare.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕從卿受經，卿從朕求官，何所疑？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I received the classics from you; you seek office from me—what doubt is there?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then said: "I received the classics from you; you seek office from me—what doubt is there?"

sentences.zh: 後胤頓首，願得國子祭酒，授之。

translations.literal: Houyin bowed his head and wished to obtain the libationership of the Directorate of Education; it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Houyin bowed his head and wished to obtain the libationership of the Directorate of Education, it was granted.

sentences.zh: 遷散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He became transferred to Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 永徽中致仕，加金紫光祿大夫，朝朔望，祿賜防閣如舊。

translations.literal: In the Yonghui era he retired from office, was additionally appointed Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon, attended on the first and fifteenth of the month, and stipends and guards were as before.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yonghui era he retired from office, was additionally appointed Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon, attended on the first and fifteenth of the month, and stipends and guards were as before.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十三，贈禮部尚書，謚曰康，陪葬昭陵。

translations.literal: He died at the age of eighty-three, was posthumously appointed Minister of Rites, given the posthumous title Kang, and buried with honor at Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty-three, was posthumously appointed Minister of Rites, given the posthumous title Kang, and buried with honor at Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 孫齊丘，歷監察御史、朔方節度使，終東都留守，謚曰貞獻。

translations.literal: His grandson Qiqiu successively served as Censor, Military Commissioner of Shuofang, and ended as Guardian of the Eastern Capital; his posthumous title was Zhenxian.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Qiqiu successively served as Censor, Military Commissioner of Shuofang, and ended as Guardian of the Eastern Capital, his posthumous title was Zhenxian.

sentences.zh: 子鎰，別有傳。

translations.literal: His son Yi has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yi is treated in a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 蓋文達，冀州信都人。

translations.literal: Gai Wenda was a native of Xindu in Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gai Wenda came from Xindu in Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 博涉前載，尤明《春秋》三家。

translations.literal: Broadly versed in earlier records, he was especially accomplished in the three traditions of the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly versed in earlier records. he was especially accomplished in the three traditions of the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 刺史竇抗集諸生講論，於是，劉焯、劉軌思、孔穎達並以耆儒開門授業，是日悉至，而文達依經辯舉，皆諸儒意所未叩，一坐厭嘆。

translations.literal: Prefect Dou Kang gathered scholars to lecture; on that day Liu Zhuo, Liu Guisi, and Kong Yingda, all venerable Confucians who opened doors to teach, all arrived; Wenda argued according to the classics on points none of the Confucians had raised— the whole assembly sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Dou Kang gathered scholars to lecture; on that day Liu Zhuo, Liu Guisi, and Kong Yingda, all venerable Confucians who opened doors to teach, all arrived; Wenda argued according to the classics on points none of the Confucians had raised—the whole assembly sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 抗奇之，問：「安所從學？」

translations.literal: Kang marveled at him and asked: "Where did you study?"
translations.idiomatic: Kang marveled at him and asked: "Where did you study?"

sentences.zh: 焯曰：「若人岐嶷，出自天然，以多問寡，則焯為之師。」

translations.literal: Zhuo said: "This man is sharp and intelligent, gifted by nature; if one asks much of the few, then Zhuo is his teacher."
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo said: "This man is sharp and intelligent, gifted by nature, if one asks much of the few, then Zhuo is his teacher."

sentences.zh: 抗曰：「冰生於水而寒於水，其謂此邪？」

translations.literal: Kang said: "Ice is born of water yet colder than water—is this not so?"
translations.idiomatic: Kang replied: "Ice is born of water yet colder than water—is this not so?"

sentences.zh: 武德中，授國子助教，為秦王文學館直學士。

translations.literal: In the Wude era he was appointed Assistant Instructor of the Directorate of Education and Direct Academician of the Literary Academy of the Prince of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wude era he was appointed Assistant Instructor of the Directorate of Education and Direct Academician of the Literary Academy of the Prince of Qin.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，擢諫議大夫、兼弘文館學士，為蜀王師。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan he was promoted to Remonstrator of the Left and concurrently academician of the Hongwen Hall, serving as teacher to the Prince of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Zhenguan period he was promoted to Remonstrator of the Left and concurrently academician of the Hongwen Hall, serving as teacher to the Prince of Shu.

sentences.zh: 王有罪，文達免官。

translations.literal: When the prince was guilty, Wenda was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince was guilty. Wenda was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 拜崇賢館學士，卒。

translations.literal: He was appointed academician of the Chongxian Hall and died.
translations.idiomatic: He became appointed academician of the Chongxian Hall and died.

sentences.zh: 宗人文懿，亦以儒學稱，當時號「二蓋」。

translations.literal: Clansman Wenyi was also renowned for Confucian learning; at the time they were styled the "Two Gai."
translations.idiomatic: His clansman Wenyi was also renowned for Confucian learning; at the time they were styled the "Two Gai."

sentences.zh: 高祖於秘書省置學以教王公子，文懿為國子助教。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu established a school at the Secretariat to teach princes' sons; Wenyi was Assistant Instructor of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu established a school at the Secretariat to teach princes' sons, Wenyi was Assistant Instructor of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 既升席，公卿更相質問，文懿譬曉密微，遠近宗仰。

translations.literal: When he ascended the mat, ministers and officials questioned one another in turn; Wenyi explained with subtle precision; near and far honored and looked up to him.
translations.idiomatic: When he ascended the mat, ministers and officials questioned one another in turn, Wenyi explained with subtle precision, near and far honored and looked up to him.

sentences.zh: 終國子博士。

translations.literal: He ended as Erudite of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He finished his career as Erudite of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 谷那律，魏州昌樂人。

translations.literal: Gu Nalü was a native of Changle in Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Nalü came from Changle in Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，累遷國子博士。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan era he was repeatedly promoted to Erudite of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguan era he was repeatedly promoted to Erudite of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 淹識群書，褚遂良嘗稱為「《九經》庫」。

translations.literal: Deeply knowing all books, Chu Suiliang once called him the "Storehouse of the Nine Classics."
translations.idiomatic: Deeply knowing all books. Chu Suiliang once called him the "Storehouse of the Nine Classics."

sentences.zh: 遷諫議大夫，兼弘文館學士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Remonstrator of the Left and concurrently academician of the Hongwen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He became transferred to Remonstrator of the Left and concurrently academician of the Hongwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 從太宗出獵，遇雨沾漬，因問曰：「油衣若為而無漏邪？」

translations.literal: Following Emperor Taizong on a hunt, he encountered rain and soaking; the emperor thereupon asked: "How is it that an oil coat does not leak?"
translations.idiomatic: When he followed Emperor Taizong on a hunt, he encountered rain and soaking; the emperor thereupon asked: "How is it that an oil coat does not leak?"

sentences.zh: 那律曰：「以瓦為之，當不漏。」

translations.literal: Nalü said: "If made of tile, it would not leak."
translations.idiomatic: Nalü said: "If made of tile. it would not leak."

sentences.zh: 帝悅其直，賜帛二百段，卒。

translations.literal: The emperor delighted in his directness and bestowed two hundred bolts of silk; he died.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor delighted in his directness and bestowed two hundred bolts of silk, he died.

sentences.zh: 孫倚相，仕為秘書省正字，讎覆圖書，多所刊定。

translations.literal: His grandson Yixiang served as Corrector of the Secretariat, collating books and correcting many points.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Yixiang served as Corrector of the Secretariat, collating books and correcting many points.

sentences.zh: 子崇義，天寶末為幽州大將，以雄敢聞。

translations.literal: His son Chongyi, at the end of the Tianbao era was a great general of Youzhou, renowned for bold courage.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chongyi. at the end of the Tianbao era was a great general of Youzhou, renowned for bold courage.

sentences.zh: 歷左金吾衛大將軍，遂客薊門。

translations.literal: He successively served as Grand General of the Left Golden Guard and then lodged as guest at Jimen.
translations.idiomatic: He successively served as Grand General of the Left Golden Guard and then lodged as guest at Jimen.

sentences.zh: 生子從政，略涉儒學，有風操。

translations.literal: He begot Congzheng, who slightly versed himself in Confucian learning and had moral conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He begot Congzheng. who slightly versed himself in Confucian learning and had moral conduct.

sentences.zh: 事李寶臣，歷定州刺史，封清江郡王。

translations.literal: Serving Li Baochen, he successively served as Prefect of Dingzhou and was enfeoffed as Prince of Qingjiang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Serving Li Baochen. he successively served as Prefect of Dingzhou and was enfeoffed as Prince of Qingjiang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 寶臣及張孝忠妻，其女兄弟也。

translations.literal: Baochen and the wife of Zhang Xiaozhong were his daughter's siblings.
translations.idiomatic: Baochen and the wife of Zhang Xiaozhong were related to him through his daughter.

sentences.zh: 寶臣初倚任，晚稍疏忌，從政乃闔門謝交遊不事。

translations.literal: Baochen at first relied on and employed him; in his later years he gradually grew distant and suspicious; Congzheng then closed his gates, declined social intercourse, and did not engage in affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Baochen at first relied on and employed him, in his later years he gradually grew distant and suspicious, Congzheng then closed his gates, declined social intercourse, and did not engage in affairs.

sentences.zh: 及惟嶽知節度，與田悅謀拒天子命，從政諫曰：「上神斷，絀諸侯，欲致太平。

translations.literal: When Wei Yue controlled the military commission and together with Tian Yue plotted to resist the Son of Heaven's command, Congzheng remonstrated: "The emperor is divinely decisive, restraining the feudal lords, wishing to bring great peace.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Yue controlled the military commission and together with Tian Yue plotted to resist the Son of Heaven's command, Congzheng remonstrated: "The emperor is divinely decisive, restraining the feudal lords, wishing to bring great peace.

sentences.zh: 爾考與燕有切骨恨，天子致討，命帥莫先於燕。

translations.literal: Your father and Yan had bone-cutting hatred; the Son of Heaven launched punishment—the command to lead troops came first to Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Your father and Yan had bone-cutting hatred, the Son of Heaven launched punishment—the command to lead troops came first to Yan.

sentences.zh: 誅怨復仇，必盡力後已。

translations.literal: To wipe out grievance and take revenge, one must exert full strength afterward.
translations.idiomatic: To wipe out grievance and take revenge. one must exert full strength afterward.

sentences.zh: 前日而考誅大將百餘，子弟存者常不平，乘危相覆，誰不能爾？

translations.literal: The other day your father executed more than a hundred great generals; surviving sons and younger brothers are often discontent—seizing crisis to overturn one another, who cannot do this?
translations.idiomatic: The other day your father executed more than a hundred great generals, surviving sons and younger brothers are often discontent—seizing crisis to overturn one another, who cannot do this?

sentences.zh: 昔魏有洺、相之圍，王師四集，身投零陵，仰天垂泣，不知所出。

translations.literal: Formerly Wei had the siege of Luozhou and Xiangzhou; imperial armies gathered from four sides; he threw himself on Lingling, looked up to Heaven and wept, not knowing where to turn.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Wei had the siege of Luozhou and Xiangzhou, imperial armies gathered from four sides, he threw himself on Lingling, looked up to Heaven and wept, not knowing where to turn.

sentences.zh: 賴爾考保佑，頓兵不進，而先帝寬厚，僅獲赦貸。

translations.literal: Relying on your father's protection, troops halted and did not advance; moreover the former emperor was generous and he barely obtained pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Relying on your father's protection, troops halted and did not advance, moreover the former emperor was generous and he barely obtained pardon.

sentences.zh: 不然，田氏尚有種乎？

translations.literal: Otherwise, would the Tian clan still have seed?
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, would the Tian clan still have any descendants at all?

sentences.zh: 今悅兇獪，孰與承嗣？

translations.literal: Now Yue is fierce and cunning—who compares with Chengsi?
translations.idiomatic: Now Yue is fierce and cunning—who compares with Chengsi?

sentences.zh: 爾又幼富貴，不出戶庭，便欲旅拒？

translations.literal: You are again young and rich, never leaving the door—yet you wish to resist as a traveler?
translations.idiomatic: You are again young and rich. never leaving the door—yet you wish to resist as a traveler?

sentences.zh: 且人心難知，天道難欺，軍中諸將乘危投隙，自古豈少哉！

translations.literal: Moreover people's hearts are hard to know, Heaven's way is hard to deceive—generals in the army seizing crisis to find openings: since antiquity are they not many?
translations.idiomatic: Furthermore, people's hearts are hard to know, Heaven's way is hard to deceive—generals in the army seizing crisis to find openings: since antiquity are they not many?

sentences.zh: 今圖久安計，莫若令而兄惟誠攝留後，爾速入宿衛，則福祿可保矣。」

translations.literal: Now for a plan of long peace, nothing surpasses having your elder brother Weicheng act as acting commissioner while you quickly enter to guard the palace—then fortune and rank can be preserved."
translations.idiomatic: Now for a plan of long peace. nothing surpasses having your elder brother Weicheng act as acting commissioner while you quickly enter to guard the palace—then fortune and rank can be preserved."

sentences.zh: 不納。

translations.literal: He did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He did not accept.

sentences.zh: 從政塞門移疾不出，惟嶽所信王他奴等疑其怨望，日伺之。

translations.literal: Congzheng shut his gate, feigned illness, and did not go out; Wang Tanu and others whom Wei Yue trusted, suspecting his resentment, daily watched him.
translations.idiomatic: Congzheng shut his gate, feigned illness, and did not go out, Wang Tanu and others whom Wei Yue trusted, suspecting his resentment, daily watched him.

sentences.zh: 從政懼，乃吐血，即仰藥，五日死。

translations.literal: Congzheng feared this and spat blood; he immediately took poison and died in five days.
translations.idiomatic: Congzheng feared this and spat blood, he immediately took poison and died in five days.

sentences.zh: 曰：「吾不恨死，而痛渠覆宗矣！」

translations.literal: He said: "I do not regret death, but grieve that the channel will overturn the clan!"
translations.idiomatic: He said: "I do not regret death. but grieve that the channel will overturn the clan!"

sentences.zh: 後惟嶽被殺於王武俊，如其揣雲。

translations.literal: Later Wei Yue was killed by Wang Wujun, just as he had foretold.
translations.idiomatic: Afterwards, Wei Yue was killed by Wang Wujun, just as he had foretold.

sentences.zh: 蕭德言，字文行，陳吏部郎引子也，系出蘭陵。

translations.literal: Xiao Deyan, styled Wenxing, was the son of Gentleman Lang of the Ministry of Personnel of Chen Yin; his lineage came from Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Deyan, styled Wenxing, was the son of Gentleman Lang of the Ministry of Personnel of Chen Yin, his lineage came from Lanling.

sentences.zh: 明《左氏春秋》。

translations.literal: He was accomplished in the Zuo clan Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered the Zuo clan Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 甫冠，以國子生為嶽陽王賓客。

translations.literal: Having just reached adulthood, as a student of the Directorate of Education he became Retainer to the Prince of Yueyang.
translations.idiomatic: Having just reached adulthood. as a student of the Directorate of Education he became Retainer to the Prince of Yueyang.

sentences.zh: 陳亡，徙關中。

translations.literal: When Chen fell he moved to Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: After Chen fell he moved to Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 詭浮屠服亡歸江南，州縣部送京師。

translations.literal: Feigning Buddhist robes he secretly returned to Jiangnan; prefectures and counties escorted him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Feigning Buddhist robes he secretly returned to Jiangnan, prefectures and counties escorted him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 仁壽中，授校書郎。

translations.literal: In the Renshou era he was appointed Proofreader.
translations.idiomatic: During the Renshou era he was appointed Proofreader.

sentences.zh: 貞觀時，歷著作郎、弘文館學士。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan era he successively served as Gentleman of the Secretariat and academician of the Hongwen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguan era he successively served as Gentleman of the Secretariat and academician of the Hongwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 太宗欲知前世得失，詔魏征、虞世南、褚亮及德言裒次經史百氏帝王所以興衰者上之，帝愛其書博而要，曰：「使我稽古臨事不惑者，公等力也！」

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong wished to know the gains and losses of former ages; he ordered Wei Zheng, Yu Shinan, Chu Liang, and Deyan to compile and arrange from the classics, histories, and records of the hundred schools how emperors rose and fell and present it; the emperor loved that the book was broad yet essential and said: "What enables me to examine antiquity and not be confused in affairs is your strength!"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong wished to know the gains and losses of former ages, he ordered Wei Zheng, Yu Shinan, Chu Liang, and Deyan to compile and arrange from the classics, histories, and records of the hundred schools how emperors rose and fell and present it, the emperor loved that the book was broad yet essential and said: "What enables me to examine antiquity and not be confused in affairs is your strength!"

sentences.zh: 賚賜尤渥。

translations.literal: Rewards and gifts were especially generous.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards and gifts were especially generous.

sentences.zh: 德言晚節學愈苦，每開經，輒祓濯束帶危坐，妻子諫曰：「老人何終日自苦？」

translations.literal: In his later years Deyan's study grew ever more arduous; whenever he opened a classic he would purify himself, gird his sash, and sit upright; his wife admonished him: "An old man—why exhaust himself daily?"
translations.idiomatic: In his later years Deyan's study grew ever more arduous, whenever he opened a classic he would purify himself, gird his sash, and sit upright, his wife admonished him: "An old man—why exhaust himself daily?"

sentences.zh: 答曰：「對先聖之言，何復憚勞？」

translations.literal: He replied: "Facing the words of the former sages—why again fear toil?"
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Facing the words of the former sages—why again fear toil?"

sentences.zh: 詔以經授晉王。

translations.literal: An edict had him instruct the Prince of Jin in the classics.
translations.idiomatic: An edict had him instruct the Prince of Jin in the classics.

sentences.zh: 時許叔牙為侍讀，同勸講。

translations.literal: At the time Xu Shuya was Reader-in-Attendance and together they urged lectures.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, Xu Shuya was Reader-in-Attendance and together they urged lectures.

sentences.zh: 王為太子，德言又兼侍讀，而叔牙亦兼弘文館學士。

translations.literal: When the prince became crown prince, Deyan again concurrently served as Reader-in-Attendance, and Shuya also concurrently served as academician of the Hongwen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince became crown prince. Deyan again concurrently served as Reader-in-Attendance, and Shuya also concurrently served as academician of the Hongwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 德言請致仕，太宗不許，下詔敦勉。

translations.literal: Deyan requested retirement; Emperor Taizong did not permit it and issued an edict earnestly encouraging him.
translations.idiomatic: Deyan requested retirement, Emperor Taizong did not permit it and issued an edict earnestly encouraging him.

sentences.zh: 封武陽縣侯，進秘書少監，久乃得謝。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wuyang, advanced to Vice Director of the Secretariat, and after a long time obtained leave.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wuyang. advanced to Vice Director of the Secretariat, and after a long time obtained leave.

sentences.zh: 高宗立，拜銀青光祿大夫，全給其祿，遣通事舍人即家致問。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong took the throne he was appointed Grand Master of the Silver Seal and Blue Ribbon, given his full stipend, and a Palace Usher was sent to his home to convey inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong took the throne he became appointed Grand Master of the Silver Seal and Blue Ribbon, given his full stipend, and a Palace Usher became sent to his home to convey inquiry.

sentences.zh: 乘輿至肅章門引見，禮遇隆重。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage arrived at Suzhang Gate and he was led in for audience; courtesy and treatment were heavy.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial carriage arrived at Suzhang Gate and he was led in for audience, courtesy and treatment were heavy.

sentences.zh: 由是晉府及東宮舊臣子孫，並增秩賜金。

translations.literal: Thereupon descendants of former retainers of the Jin Princely Establishment and Eastern Palace all received increased rank and bestowed gold.
translations.idiomatic: Then descendants of former retainers of the Jin Princely Establishment and Eastern Palace all received increased rank and bestowed gold.

sentences.zh: 卒，年九十七，贈太常卿，謚曰博。

translations.literal: He died at the age of ninety-seven, was posthumously appointed Minister of Ceremonies, and given the posthumous title Bo.
translations.idiomatic: He died at ninety-seven, was posthumously appointed Minister of Ceremonies, and given the posthumous title Bo.

sentences.zh: 叔牙，字延基，句容人。

translations.literal: Shuya, styled Yanji, was a native of Jurong.
translations.idiomatic: Shuya. styled Yanji, was a native of Jurong.

sentences.zh: 貞觀時，遷晉王府參軍事、弘文館直學士。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan era he was transferred to Administrative Assistant in the Princely Household of Jin and Direct Academician of the Hongwen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguan era he was transferred to Administrative Assistant in the Princely Household of Jin and Direct Academician of the Hongwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 於《詩》、《禮》尤邃，獻《詩纂義》十篇，太子寫付司經。

translations.literal: He was especially accomplished in the Odes and Rites; he presented ten chapters of Shizhuanyi; the crown prince copied and forwarded them to the Directorate of Classics.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially accomplished in the Odes and Rites, he presented ten chapters of Shizhuanyi, the crown prince copied and forwarded them to the Directorate of Classics.

sentences.zh: 御史大夫高智周見之曰：「欲明《詩》者，宜先讀此。」

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Gao Zhizhou saw them and said: "Those who wish to clarify the Odes should first read this."
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Gao Zhizhou saw them and replied: "Those who wish to clarify the Odes should first read this."

sentences.zh: 子子儒，字文舉。

translations.literal: His son Ziru, styled Wenzju.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ziru. styled Wenzju.

sentences.zh: 高宗時為奉常博士。

translations.literal: In Emperor Gaozong's time he was Erudite of the Ministry of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Gaozong's time he became Erudite of the Ministry of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 初，太尉長孫無忌等議：「祠令及禮用鄭玄六天說，圓丘祀昊天上帝，南郊太微感帝，明堂太微五帝。

translations.literal: At first Grand Preceptor Zhangsun Wuji and others debated: "The sacrificial ordinances and rites use Zheng Xuan's Six Heaven theory—the Round Mound sacrifices to August Heaven on High, the southern suburb to the Supreme Microcosm and Sensitivity Emperor, the Bright Hall to the Supreme Microcosm Five Emperors.
translations.idiomatic: At first Grand Preceptor Zhangsun Wuji and others debated: "The sacrificial ordinances and rites use Zheng Xuan's Six Heaven theory—the Round Mound sacrifices to August Heaven on High, the southern suburb to the Supreme Microcosm and Sensitivity Emperor, the Bright Hall to the Supreme Microcosm Five Emperors.

sentences.zh: 直據緯為說，不指蒼旻為天，而以昊天帝當北辰耀魄寶，郊、明堂當太微五帝。

translations.literal: Directly relying on apocrypha as explanation, they do not point to the azure sky as Heaven, but take August Heaven on High as the North Star, Splendorous Soul Treasure; suburb and Bright Hall correspond to the Supreme Microcosm Five Emperors.
translations.idiomatic: Directly relying on apocrypha as explanation, they do not point to the azure sky as Heaven, but take August Heaven on High as the North Star, Splendorous Soul Treasure, suburb and Bright Hall correspond to the Supreme Microcosm Five Emperors.

sentences.zh: 唐家祀圓丘，太史所上圖，昊天上帝外自有北辰。

translations.literal: When Tang sacrifices at the Round Mound, the chart submitted by the Grand Astrologer shows that outside August Heaven on High there is separately the North Star.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang sacrifices at the Round Mound. the chart submitted by the Grand Astrologer shows that outside August Heaven on High there is separately the North Star.

sentences.zh: 令李淳風曰：『昊天上帝位於壇，北辰、鬥列第二垓。』

translations.literal: Director Li Chunfeng said: 'August Heaven on High occupies the altar; North Star and Dipper rank in the second terrace.'
translations.idiomatic: Director Li Chunfeng said: 'August Heaven on High occupies the altar, North Star and Dipper rank in the second terrace.'

sentences.zh: 與緯書駁異。

translations.literal: This differs from apocryphal books.
translations.idiomatic: This conflicts with the apocryphal texts.

sentences.zh: 司馬遷《天官書》，太微宮五精之神，五星所奉，有人主象，故名曰帝，猶房、心有天王象，安得盡為天乎？

translations.literal: Sima Qian's Treatise on the Heavenly Offices: the Five Essence spirits of the Supreme Microcosm Palace are attended by the five planets and have the image of a human lord—therefore they are called emperors; it is like the Heart and Room having the image of a heavenly king—how can they all be Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: Sima Qian's Treatise on the Heavenly Offices: the Five Essence spirits of the Supreme Microcosm Palace are attended by the five planets and have the image of a human lord—therefore they are called emperors, it is like the Heart and Room having the image of a heavenly king—how can they all be Heaven?

sentences.zh: 日月麗於天，草木麗於地，以日月為天，草木為地，昧者不信也。

translations.literal: Sun and moon are attached to Heaven, grass and trees are attached to earth—if one takes sun and moon as Heaven and grass and trees as earth, the ignorant do not believe.
translations.idiomatic: Sun and moon are attached to Heaven. grass and trees are attached to earth—if one takes sun and moon as Heaven and grass and trees as earth, the ignorant do not believe.

sentences.zh: 《周官》『兆五帝四郊』，又有『祀五帝』，皆不言天，知太微之神，非天也。

translations.literal: The Offices of Zhou 'establish the Five Emperors at the four suburbs' and also has 'sacrifice to the Five Emperors'—neither speaks of Heaven; one knows the spirits of the Supreme Microcosm are not Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The Offices of Zhou 'establish the Five Emperors at the four suburbs' and also has 'sacrifice to the Five Emperors'—neither speaks of Heaven, one knows the spirits of the Supreme Microcosm are not Heaven.

sentences.zh: 《經》稱『郊祀後稷』，王肅以郊、圓丘為一，玄析而二之，曰圓丘，曰郊，非聖人意。

translations.literal: The Classic says 'the suburb sacrifice follows Houji'; Wang Su takes suburb and Round Mound as one—Xuan divides them into two, saying Round Mound, saying suburb; this is not the sage's intent.
translations.idiomatic: The Classic says 'the suburb sacrifice follows Houji', Wang Su takes suburb and Round Mound as one—Xuan divides them into two, saying Round Mound, saying suburb, this is not the sage's intent.

sentences.zh: 今祠令固守玄說，與著式相違，宜有刊正。

translations.literal: Now the sacrificial ordinances rigidly adhere to Xuan's theory, contrary to established forms—it should be revised.
translations.idiomatic: Now the sacrificial ordinances rigidly adhere to Xuan's theory, contrary to established forms—it should be revised.

sentences.zh: 且《經》『嚴父莫大於配天』，『宗祀文王於明堂，以配上帝』。

translations.literal: Moreover the Classic 'honoring the father—nothing greater than matching Heaven' and 'sacrificing to King Wen in the Bright Hall to match August Heaven on High.'
translations.idiomatic: Furthermore, the Classic 'honoring the father—nothing greater than matching Heaven' and 'sacrificing to King Wen in the Bright Hall to match August Heaven on High.'

sentences.zh: 明堂之祀，天也，星不足配之矣。

translations.literal: Bright Hall sacrifice is Heaven; stars are insufficient to match it.
translations.idiomatic: Bright Hall sacrifice is Heaven, stars are insufficient to match it.

sentences.zh: 《月令》『孟春祈谷上帝』，《春秋》『啟蟄而郊，郊而後耕』，故郊後稷以祈農，《詩》『春夏祈谷於上帝』，皆祭天也。

translations.literal: Monthly Ordinance 'in the first month of spring pray for grain to August Heaven on High'; Spring and Autumn Annals 'when insects stir then suburb, after suburb then plowing'—therefore the suburb follows Houji to pray for agriculture; the Odes 'in spring and summer pray for grain to August Heaven on High'—all are sacrificing to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Monthly Ordinance 'in the first month of spring pray for grain to August Heaven on High', Spring and Autumn Annals 'when insects stir then suburb, after suburb then plowing'—therefore the suburb follows Houji to pray for agriculture, the Odes 'in spring and summer pray for grain to August Heaven on High'—all are sacrificing to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 著之感帝，尤為不稽。

translations.literal: Making it the Sensitivity Emperor is especially unexamined.
translations.idiomatic: Making it the Sensitivity Emperor is especially unexamined.

sentences.zh: 請四郊迎氣祀太微五帝，郊、明堂罷六天說，止祀昊天。

translations.literal: We request at the four suburbs welcoming qi to sacrifice to the Supreme Microcosm Five Emperors; at suburb and Bright Hall abolish the Six Heaven theory and sacrifice only to August Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: We request at the four suburbs welcoming qi to sacrifice to the Supreme Microcosm Five Emperors, at suburb and Bright Hall abolish the Six Heaven theory and sacrifice only to August Heaven.

sentences.zh: 方丘既祭地，又祭神州北郊，皆不載經，請止一祠。」

translations.literal: The Square Mound already sacrifices to earth and also sacrifices to Divine Land at the northern suburb—neither is recorded in the classics; we request stopping at one sacrifice."
translations.idiomatic: The Square Mound already sacrifices to earth and also sacrifices to Divine Land at the northern suburb—neither is recorded in the classics, we request stopping at one sacrifice."

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「可。」

translations.literal: The edict said: "Approved."
translations.idiomatic: The edict replied: "Approved."

sentences.zh: 乾封初，帝已封禪，復詔祀感帝、神州，以正月祭北郊。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Qianfeng era the emperor had already performed feng and shan; he again ordered sacrifice to the Sensitivity Emperor and Divine Land, with sacrifice at the northern suburb in the first month.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Qianfeng era the emperor had already performed feng and shan, he again ordered sacrifice to the Sensitivity Emperor and Divine Land, with sacrifice at the northern suburb in the first month.

sentences.zh: 司禮少常伯郝處俊等奏言：「顯慶定禮，廢感帝祀而祈谷昊天，以高祖配。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Ministry of Ceremonies Hao Chujun and others memorialized: "The Xianqing fixed rites abolished sacrifice to the Sensitivity Emperor and prayed for grain to August Heaven on High, with Emperor Gaozu as correlate.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Ministry of Ceremonies Hao Chujun and others memorialized: "The Xianqing fixed rites abolished sacrifice to the Sensitivity Emperor and prayed for grain to August Heaven on High, with Emperor Gaozu as correlate.

sentences.zh: 舊祀感帝、神州，以元皇帝配。

translations.literal: Formerly the Sensitivity Emperor and Divine Land were sacrificed to with the Primordial Emperor as correlate.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly the Sensitivity Emperor and Divine Land were sacrificed to with the Primordial Emperor as correlate.

sentences.zh: 今改祈谷為祀感帝，又祀神州，還以高祖配，何升降紛紛焉？

translations.literal: Now changing prayer for grain to sacrifice to the Sensitivity Emperor and again sacrificing to Divine Land, yet again using Emperor Gaozu as correlate—why such rising and falling confusion?
translations.idiomatic: Now changing prayer for grain to sacrifice to the Sensitivity Emperor and again sacrificing to Divine Land, yet again using Emperor Gaozu as correlate—why such rising and falling confusion?

sentences.zh: 虞氏禘黃帝，郊嚳；

translations.literal: Yu di performed di to the Yellow Emperor and jiao to Ku;
translations.idiomatic: Yu di performed di to the Yellow Emperor and jiao to Ku;

sentences.zh: 夏禘黃帝，郊鯀；

translations.literal: Xia performed di to the Yellow Emperor and jiao to Gun;
translations.idiomatic: Xia performed di to the Yellow Emperor and jiao to Gun;

sentences.zh: 殷禘嚳，郊冥；

translations.literal: Yin performed di to Ku and jiao to Ming;
translations.idiomatic: Yin performed di to Ku and jiao to Ming;

sentences.zh: 周禘嚳，郊稷。

translations.literal: Zhou performed di to Ku and jiao to Houji.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou performed di to Ku and jiao to Houji.

sentences.zh: 玄謂禘者，祭天圓丘；

translations.literal: Xuan says di is sacrificing to Heaven at the Round Mound;
translations.idiomatic: Xuan says di is sacrificing to Heaven at the Round Mound;

sentences.zh: 郊者，祭上帝南郊。

translations.literal: jiao is sacrificing to August Heaven on High at the southern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: jiao is sacrificing to August Heaven on High at the southern suburb.

sentences.zh: 崔靈恩說夏正郊天，王者各祭所出帝，所謂『王者禘祖之所自出，以其祖配之』。

translations.literal: Cui Lingen's theory: at the first month of Xia the Son of Heaven performs suburban sacrifice to Heaven; each king sacrifices to the emperor from whom he issued—this is what is meant by 'the king performs di to the ancestor from whom he issued and matches his ancestor to him.'
translations.idiomatic: Cui Lingen's theory: at the first month of Xia the Son of Heaven performs suburban sacrifice to Heaven, each king sacrifices to the emperor from whom he issued—this is what is meant by 'the king performs di to the ancestor from whom he issued and matches his ancestor to him.'

sentences.zh: 則禘遠祖，郊始祖也。

translations.literal: Thus di is the distant ancestor; jiao is the founding ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Thus di is the distant ancestor, jiao is the founding ancestor.

sentences.zh: 今禘、郊同祖，禮無所歸。

translations.literal: Now di and jiao share the same ancestor—there is nowhere for the rite to return.
translations.idiomatic: Now di and jiao share the same ancestor—there is nowhere for the rite to return.

sentences.zh: 神州本祭十月，以方陰用事也。

translations.literal: Divine Land originally was sacrificed to in the tenth month, when the yin force was in charge.
translations.idiomatic: Divine Land originally became sacrificed to in the tenth month, when the yin force became in charge.

sentences.zh: 玄說三王之郊，一用夏正。

translations.literal: Xuan's theory of the three kings' suburban sacrifices all used the first month of Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan's theory of the three kings' suburban sacrifices all used the first month of Xia.

sentences.zh: 靈恩謂祭神州北郊，以正月。

translations.literal: Lingen says sacrificing to Divine Land at the northern suburb uses the first month.
translations.idiomatic: Lingen says sacrificing to Divine Land at the northern suburb uses the first month.

sentences.zh: 諸儒所言，猥互不明。

translations.literal: What the Confucians say is confused and unclear.
translations.idiomatic: What the Confucians say is confused and unclear.

sentences.zh: 臣願會奉常、司成、博士普議。」

translations.literal: Your subject wishes to convene the Director of Ceremonies, Vice Director of Education, and erudites for general debate."
translations.idiomatic: Your subject wishes to convene the Director of Ceremonies, Vice Director of Education, and erudites for general debate."

sentences.zh: 於是，子儒與博士陸遵楷、張統師、權無二等共白：「北郊月不經見，漢光武正月建北郊，鹹和中議北郊以正月，武德以來用十月，請循武德詔書。」

translations.literal: Thereupon Ziru together with Erudites Lu Zunkai, Zhang Tongshi, Quan Wuer, and others jointly stated: "The northern suburb month is not seen in the classics; Han Emperor Guangwu in the first month established the northern suburb; in the Xianhe era they debated the northern suburb in the first month; since Wude the tenth month has been used—we request following the Wude edict."
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Ziru together with Erudites Lu Zunkai, Zhang Tongshi, Quan Wuer, and others jointly stated: "The northern suburb month is not seen in the classics, Han Emperor Guangwu in the first month established the northern suburb, in the Xianhe era they debated the northern suburb in the first month, since Wude the tenth month has been used—we request following the Wude edict."

sentences.zh: 明年，詔圓方二丘、明堂、感帝、神州宜奉高祖、太宗配，仍祭昊天上帝及五天帝於明堂。

translations.literal: The next year an edict ordered the Round and Square Mounds, Bright Hall, Sensitivity Emperor, and Divine Land to have Emperor Gaozu and Emperor Taizong as correlates, and still to sacrifice to August Heaven on High and the Five August Emperors at the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The next year an edict ordered the Round and Square Mounds, Bright Hall, Sensitivity Emperor, and Divine Land to have Emperor Gaozu and Emperor Taizong as correlates, and still to sacrifice to August Heaven on High and the Five August Emperors at the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 子儒，長壽中，歷天官侍郎、弘文館學士，封潁川縣男。

translations.literal: Ziru, in the Changshou era, successively served as Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel and academician of the Hongwen Hall, and was enfeoffed as Baron of Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Ziru. in the Changshou era, successively served as Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel and academician of the Hongwen Hall, and was enfeoffed as Baron of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 以選事委令史句直，日偃臥不下筆，時人語曰「句直平配」。

translations.literal: He entrusted selection affairs to clerk Gou Zhi; daily he lay down and did not pick up the brush—men of the time said "Gou Zhi decides appointments."
translations.idiomatic: He entrusted selection affairs to clerk Gou Zhi, daily he lay down and did not pick up the brush—men of the time said "Gou Zhi decides appointments."

sentences.zh: 既而補授失序，傳為口實。

translations.literal: Before long supplementary appointments lost order and became a byword.
translations.idiomatic: Before long supplementary appointments lost order and became proverbial.

sentences.zh: 德言曾孫至忠，自有傳。

translations.literal: Deyan's great-grandson Zhizhong has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Deyan's great-grandson Zhizhong is given a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 敬播，蒲州河東人。

translations.literal: Jing Bo was a native of Hedong in Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Bo came from Hedong in Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，擢進士第。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Zhenguan period he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 時顏師古、孔穎達撰次《隋史》，詔播詣秘書內省參纂。

translations.literal: At the time Yan Shigu and Kong Yingda were compiling the History of Sui; an edict ordered Bo to go to the inner Secretariat to participate in compilation.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, Yan Shigu and Kong Yingda were compiling the History of Sui; an edict ordered Bo to go to the inner Secretariat to participate in compilation.

sentences.zh: 再遷著作佐郎，兼修國史。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Assistant Gentleman of the Secretariat and concurrently revised the National History.
translations.idiomatic: He became again transferred to Assistant Gentleman of the Secretariat and concurrently revised the National History.

sentences.zh: 從太宗伐高麗，而帝名所戰山為駐蹕，播謂人曰：「鑾輿不復東矣，山所以名，蓋天意也！」

translations.literal: Following Emperor Taizong's campaign against Goguryeo, the emperor named the mountain where they fought Zhubi; Bo said to people: "The imperial carriage will not again go east—the mountain's name, I suppose, is Heaven's intent!"
translations.idiomatic: Following Emperor Taizong's campaign against Goguryeo, the emperor named the mountain where they fought Zhubi, Bo said to people: "The imperial carriage will not again go east—the mountain's name, I suppose, is Heaven's intent!"

sentences.zh: 其後果然。

translations.literal: Afterwards it was indeed so.
translations.idiomatic: Events later proved him right.

sentences.zh: 遷太子司議郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Remonstrator of the Crown Prince.
